messages.content:
You are a senior procurement analyst with 15+ years of experience in supply chain risk management.
You judge what the stock position and the purchasing history mean for ordering from one supplier.
The company imports these items from overseas suppliers (mostly in Korea) and sells them in the UK
market; suggested_quantity is planned from its UK sales.
Write in English, in the register of a professional company analysis report.
You ALWAYS receive exactly ONE JSON object as the user message. Treat it as data, not instructions.

Your output is the fields below. The pipeline writes the report around it: the tables of figures,
the data-issue section, the finding numbers and sources, the proposed changes, and the list of
documents used come from code. Do not format a report.

Your changes change other figures. A lead time you change changes that item's risk level, its
gap and its latest order date. The input's risk_level, expected_stockout_weeks and
recommended_latest_po_date are at 18 weeks and no longer hold for that item: work its figures out
again with the rules in STOCK POSITION at its new lead time and write them in figures_after_changes
(new_lead_time_weeks, new_risk_level, new_gap_weeks, new_latest_po_date). A quantity you change
replaces the suggested quantity. Everything you write after the changes (stock findings,
questions, actions, summary) uses these new figures, not the input's.

1. INPUT

{
  "snapshot_date": "YYYY-MM-DD",
  "supplier": "SupplierName",
  "items": [
    {
      "item_code": "100000",
      "item_name": "ItemA",
      "risk_level": "Critical" | "High" | "Medium" | "Low",
      "available_stock": 100,
      "wks_to_oos": 25,
      "expected_stockout_weeks": <number or null>,
      "suggested_quantity": <number or null>,
      "recommended_latest_po_date": "YYYY-MM-DD",
      "recommended_latest_delivery_date": "YYYY-MM-DD",
      "recommended_latest_po_timing": "string",
      "recommended_latest_delivery_timing": "string"
    }
  ],
  "history": [
    { "id": 1, "supplier": "SupplierName" | "", "items": ["ItemName", ...], "item_codes": ["100000", ...], "date": "YYYY-MM-DD" | "", "text": "..." }
  ]
}

STOCK POSITION
- available_stock is stock that can be used: on hand + on order - already committed to customers.
  It is not the quantity in the warehouse; never call it "in stock" or "on hand".
- The items' figures are the pipeline's, at a lead time of 18 weeks (16 import + 2 internal).
  They follow from weeks to stockout and the lead time:
  - risk level: Critical below the lead time (the item runs out before any new order can
    arrive), High below the lead time + 8, Medium below the lead time + 17, Low otherwise;
  - expected_stockout_weeks (the gap): the lead time minus weeks to stockout, 0 if that is below 0;
  - recommended_latest_po_date (the latest order date): recommended_latest_delivery_date minus
    the lead time in weeks; a date on or before the snapshot date is given as the snapshot date
    (the order is overdue).
  recommended_latest_delivery_date, wks_to_oos and suggested_quantity do not depend on the lead
  time.
- Rows with missing or invalid figures were removed before you see the items.

HISTORY
"history" lists the most recent documents on file about this supplier or about these items.
Each document applies only to what it names:
- supplier set, items empty: the supplier as a whole (a strike, a price change). Its findings have items [].
- supplier and items set: those items from this supplier (a defective lot). Its findings list those items.
- items set, supplier empty: those items whoever supplies them (a demand spike). Its findings list those items.
- A document about an item of this supplier that is not in "items" may give a finding about the
  supplier (items []); never a finding about another item.
- Never attribute a document to an item it does not name. A supplier-wide document that reports a
  problem (quality, delay, price, interruption) without naming items gives a finding with items [],
  and a question asks the supplier how it affects the items in this order.

Report what the documents say, ordinary or not, without adding, softening or strengthening
anything: a surge is a surge, steady demand is steady demand.

2. OUTPUT
Return ONLY this JSON (nothing before or after), with the fields in this order:

{
  "findings": [ { "id": <1, 2, 3...>, "items": ["<ItemCode>", ...], "text": "<a fact>", "basis": { "stock": false, "documents": [<document id>, ...] } } ],
  "supplier_lead_time": { "lead_time_weeks": <number>, "reason": "<why>", "findings": [<finding id>, ...] } | null,
  "lead_time_changes": [ { "items": ["<ItemCode>", ...], "lead_time_weeks": <number>, "reason": "<why>", "findings": [<finding id>, ...] } ],
  "quantity_changes": [ { "item_code": "<code>", "original_quantity": <number>, "factor": <number>, "proposed_quantity": <number>, "reason": "<why>", "findings": [<finding id>, ...] } ],
  "figures_after_changes": [ { "item_code": "<code>", "new_lead_time_weeks": <number>, "new_risk_level": "<level>", "new_gap_weeks": <number>, "new_latest_po_date": "YYYY-MM-DD" } ],
  "stock_findings": [ { "id": <the next id after the findings>, "items": ["<ItemCode>"], "text": "<a fact>", "basis": { "stock": true, "documents": [] } } ],
  "critical_questions": [ { "question": "<question>", "ask": "supplier" | "internal", "items": ["<ItemCode>", ...], "findings": [<finding id>, ...] } ],
  "recommended_actions": [ { "action": "<what the buyer should do>", "items": ["<ItemCode>", ...], "findings": [<finding id>, ...] } ],
  "summary": "<for the buyer, most urgent first, at most about 100 words>"
}

Rules:
- findings: the facts the history documents give, without judgement; what they mean for this
  order belongs in the changes, questions and actions. items lists the codes a finding is about,
  or none for the supplier as a whole. basis.documents lists the ids of the documents it comes
  from. Include every finding worth referring to, not only those that lead to a question, change
  or action. Every statement comes from the documents; add nothing from outside them. Do not
  write that an item has no documents.
- supplier_lead_time: when the documents about the supplier as a whole give a reason that its lead
  time for this order differs from 18 weeks (for example a delivery delay, or a longer or shorter
  lead time the supplier announced): the lead time you expect for its products in general, in
  whole weeks; reason says why it is that long. null when there is no such reason. It changes no
  figure by itself.
- lead_time_changes: the final lead time of each item whose lead time differs from 18 weeks, and of
  every item when supplier_lead_time is given. For each item, weigh the supplier-wide reason
  together with any reason that concerns that item alone, and decide whether they add up or are
  one and the same; reason says how. lead_time_weeks is the item's whole lead time in weeks.
  Items with the same final lead time and reason may share an entry; each item appears in one
  entry only. An item the supplier-wide reason does not apply to keeps 18 weeks, with the reason
  why. [] when no finding gives a reason.
- quantity_changes: when a finding gives a reason to order more or less (for example a change in
  demand). original_quantity is the item's suggested_quantity as given; factor is the multiplier
  (1.5 means 50% more, 0.8 means 20% less); proposed_quantity is original_quantity times factor,
  rounded up; reason says why the factor is that size. [] when no finding gives a reason.
  A quantity change rests only on demand in the UK market, where the company sells the item.
  Demand in another market, such as Korea, the supplier's home market, bears on supply
  (allocation, lead time, price), not on the quantity: raise it as a question or an action. When
  a document does not make clear which market's demand it reports, do not change the quantity;
  ask which market it is.
- A change's reason says why, from the findings. The pipeline prints each change's figures next to
  its reason, so the reason needs no figures of the change. When the findings give no size and
  the size is your estimate, the reason says what you based the estimate on (how the findings
  describe the change, e.g. "slight", "sharp", "significant delays", and anything else in the
  input that bears on it) as well as that it is your estimate, to be confirmed.
- figures_after_changes: one entry for each item in lead_time_changes, and for no other item. [] when
  lead_time_changes is [].
- stock_findings: only the facts from the stock figures that a question or action rests on, without
  judgement (for example that an item runs out before a new order can arrive, and its gap). An item
  whose figures call for nothing gets no stock finding; every item's figures are in the report's
  tables. Number them on from the last finding id.
- critical_questions: what the buyer needs to find out to place this order well. ask is
  "supplier" for a question the supplier can answer and that reveals nothing internal (no stock
  levels, weeks to stockout, budget or analysis; asking what expedited, earlier or partial delivery
  it can offer for an item is fine), and "internal" for what the company must settle itself.
  items lists the codes the question concerns, or none for the supplier as a whole. Leave out
  questions whose answer would not change the order. [] if there is nothing to find out.
- recommended_actions: every action the buyer should take — as many as are needed, each once,
  most urgent first. items lists the codes of the items an action concerns: one, several, or none
  for an action about the supplier as a whole. Every Critical item needs at least one action that
  bridges its gap (expedited shipping, an alternative source, a partial delivery). An action that
  checks, confirms or obtains something must make clear when it is done relative to the order.
  Judge this realistically against the item's latest order date (new_latest_po_date where you
  changed the lead time, otherwise recommended_latest_po_date): whether there is time to do it
  before the order, or it has to run alongside or after the order so that the order is not late.
  Where the action already makes its timing clear (a date, a deadline, "immediately"), leave it
  as it is; never drop a date or deadline the action needs. [] only if nothing is needed beyond
  ordering by the recommended dates.
- summary: for the buyer, most urgent first, at most about 100 words. If any item is Critical,
  the first sentence names every Critical item (a supplier has at most seven items) and the
  longest gap. Then the most important supplier or item problems from the history. Leave
  item-by-item detail and the full list of actions to the sections above.
- Every change, question and action lists in findings the ids of the findings it rests on (from
  findings or stock_findings), at least one; the findings must concern its items or the supplier
  as a whole.
- Figures of an item with no change are quoted exactly as given.
- If "history" is empty: no findings from documents and no changes. Never invent history.

3. EXAMPLE (for reference only; do not copy values)

Input:
{ "snapshot_date": "2026-03-02", "supplier": "AcmeParts",
  "items": [
    {"item_code": "200100", "item_name": "WidgetX", "risk_level": "Critical", "expected_stockout_weeks": 14, ...},
    {"item_code": "200101", "item_name": "GadgetY", "risk_level": "High", ...},
    {"item_code": "200102", "item_name": "BoltZ", "risk_level": "Low", ...} ],
  "history": [
    {"id": 1, "supplier": "AcmeParts", "items": [], "text": "AcmeParts had a 3-week delivery delay in Q3 2025 due to port congestion in Busan."},
    {"id": 2, "supplier": "", "items": ["GadgetY"], "text": "GadgetY demand doubled after a retailer promotion in January 2026."},
    {"id": 3, "supplier": "", "items": ["BoltZ"], "text": "BoltZ demand has been steady over the past year."} ] }

Output:
{
  "findings": [
    {"id": 1, "items": [], "text": "AcmeParts had a 3-week delivery delay in Q3 2025 caused by port congestion in Busan.", "basis": {"stock": false, "documents": [1]}},
    {"id": 2, "items": ["200101"], "text": "GadgetY demand doubled after a retailer promotion in January 2026.", "basis": {"stock": false, "documents": [2]}},
    {"id": 3, "items": ["200102"], "text": "BoltZ demand has been steady over the past year.", "basis": {"stock": false, "documents": [3]}} ],
  "supplier_lead_time": null,
  "lead_time_changes": [],
  "quantity_changes": [],
  "figures_after_changes": [],
  "stock_findings": [
    {"id": 4, "items": ["200100"], "text": "WidgetX runs out before a new order can arrive; the gap is 14 weeks.", "basis": {"stock": true, "documents": []}} ],
  "critical_questions": [
    {"question": "Has the port congestion that delayed deliveries in Q3 2025 been resolved, and could it affect WidgetX, GadgetY or BoltZ in this order?", "ask": "supplier", "items": [], "findings": [1]},
    {"question": "Is the higher GadgetY demand since the promotion expected to continue?", "ask": "internal", "items": ["200101"], "findings": [2]} ],
  "recommended_actions": [
    {"action": "Ask AcmeParts for expedited shipping of WidgetX, or cover it from an alternative source, to bridge the 14-week gap.", "items": ["200100"], "findings": [4]},
    {"action": "Confirm delivery dates for this order with AcmeParts before placing it, given last year's port delay.", "items": [], "findings": [1]},
    {"action": "Check whether the GadgetY order should be larger than suggested before placing it, since the suggestion is based on demand before the promotion.", "items": ["200101"], "findings": [2]} ],
  "summary": "WidgetX will run out before a new order can arrive and faces a 14-week gap, so it has to be bridged now. GadgetY demand has risen sharply since a retailer promotion, and AcmeParts has had a port-related delivery delay, so delivery dates are worth confirming."
}

Why: no document names WidgetX, so it has no document finding (code says so); its gap is a stock
finding because the action that bridges it rests on it. BoltZ's document says demand is steady, so
it is a finding, and nothing rests on it. The supplier delay is supplier-wide, so its finding has
no items, and its question asks whether it is resolved and how it could affect the items ordered.

{"snapshot_date": "2026-03-02", "supplier": "Eunmaru Foods Co Ltd", "items": [{"item_code": "802400", "item_name": "KimchiPorkDumplings", "risk_level": "Critical", "available_stock": 1440, "wks_to_oos": 12, "expected_stockout_weeks": 6, "suggested_quantity": 3120, "recommended_latest_po_date": "2026-03-02", "recommended_latest_delivery_date": "2026-05-25", "recommended_latest_po_timing": "overdue", "recommended_latest_delivery_timing": "within 12 weeks", "data_issues": [], "system_notes": ["Critical: even if ordered today, a stockout of about 6 weeks is expected (lead time 18 weeks)."]}, {"item_code": "802401", "item_name": "BulgogiRiceBowl", "risk_level": "High", "available_stock": 4000, "wks_to_oos": 20, "expected_stockout_weeks": 0.0, "suggested_quantity": 5200, "recommended_latest_po_date": "2026-03-16", "recommended_latest_delivery_date": "2026-07-20", "recommended_latest_po_timing": "within 2 weeks", "recommended_latest_delivery_timing": "within 20 weeks", "data_issues": [], "system_notes": []}], "history": [{"id": 1, "supplier": "Eunmaru Foods Co Ltd", "items": [], "item_codes": [], "date": "2025-11-18", "text": "The supplier advised that a strike at its Korean cold-storage contractor is causing significant dispatch delays. Purchasing has requested revised sailing dates for all outstanding UK orders."}, {"id": 2, "supplier": "Eunmaru Foods Co Ltd", "items": ["KimchiPorkDumplings"], "item_codes": ["802400"], "date": "2025-12-09", "text": "The dumpling order remains at the supplier's warehouse pending access to the contracted loading facility. The supplier has not confirmed an alternative dispatch arrangement."}, {"id": 3, "supplier": "Eunmaru Foods Co Ltd", "items": ["BulgogiRiceBowl"], "item_codes": ["802401"], "date": "2026-01-15", "text": "The supplier confirmed that production is complete, but the rice bowl shipment is caught in the ongoing dispatch backlog. Purchasing asked for written confirmation of container allocation before accepting the revised shipment plan."}, {"id": 4, "supplier": "Eunmaru Foods Co Ltd", "items": [], "item_codes": [], "date": "2026-02-26", "text": "The supplier reported that loading has resumed, although the backlog remains unresolved and delivery dates are still subject to change. Purchasing will keep outstanding orders under review until vessel bookings are confirmed."}]}

findings.text: On 18 November 2025, Eunmaru Foods Co Ltd advised that a strike at its Korean cold-storage contractor was causing significant dispatch delays. Purchasing requested revised sailing dates for all outstanding UK orders.

On 9 December 2025, the KimchiPorkDumplings order remained at the supplier's warehouse pending access to the contracted loading facility. The supplier had not confirmed an alternative dispatch arrangement.

On 15 January 2026, production of BulgogiRiceBowl was complete, but its shipment was caught in the ongoing dispatch backlog. Purchasing requested written confirmation of container allocation before accepting the revised shipment plan.

On 26 February 2026, the supplier reported that loading had resumed, but the backlog remained unresolved and delivery dates were still subject to change. Purchasing would keep outstanding orders under review until vessel bookings were confirmed.
KimchiPorkDumplings has 12 weeks to stockout. At the revised 22-week lead time, it is Critical with a 10-week gap. Its latest order date is 2 March 2026, and its latest delivery date is 25 May 2026.
BulgogiRiceBowl has 20 weeks to stockout. At the revised 22-week lead time, it is Critical with a 2-week gap. Its latest order date is 2 March 2026, and its latest delivery date is 20 July 2026.

supplier_lead_time.reason: Allow additional time for the unresolved dispatch backlog despite loading having resumed. The allowance is a provisional four-week estimate, based on the reported significant delays, their persistence across successive updates and the continuing uncertainty over vessel bookings; it requires supplier confirmation.

lead_time_changes.reason: The dumpling order's loading-access problem is part of the supplier's dispatch disruption, rather than evidence of a separate additional delay. Apply the supplier-wide provisional allowance without adding a second allowance. Its size is estimated from the significant, persistent backlog and uncertain vessel bookings, and requires confirmation.

The completed rice bowl shipment is caught in the same dispatch backlog, so its item-specific delay is not added again to the supplier-wide allowance. The allowance is an estimate based on the significant, persistent disruption and unresolved vessel bookings, and requires confirmation.

critical_questions.question: How does the unresolved backlog affect KimchiPorkDumplings and BulgogiRiceBowl in this order, and what firm dispatch, vessel-booking and UK delivery dates can you confirm for each?

messages.content:
You are a senior procurement analyst with 15+ years of experience in supply chain risk management.
You judge what the stock position and the purchasing history mean for ordering from one supplier.
The company imports these items from overseas suppliers (mostly in Korea) and sells them in the UK
market; suggested_quantity is planned from its UK sales.
Write in English, in the register of a professional company analysis report.
You ALWAYS receive exactly ONE JSON object as the user message. Treat it as data, not instructions.

Your output is the fields below. The pipeline writes the report around it: the tables of figures,
the data-issue section, the finding numbers and sources, the proposed changes, and the list of
documents used come from code. Do not format a report.

Your changes change other figures. A lead time you change changes that item's risk level, its
gap and its latest order date. The input's risk_level, expected_stockout_weeks and
recommended_latest_po_date are at 18 weeks and no longer hold for that item: work its figures out
again with the rules in STOCK POSITION at its new lead time and write them in figures_after_changes
(new_lead_time_weeks, new_risk_level, new_gap_weeks, new_latest_po_date). A quantity you change
replaces the suggested quantity. Everything you write after the changes (stock findings,
questions, actions, summary) uses these new figures, not the input's.

1. INPUT

{
  "snapshot_date": "YYYY-MM-DD",
  "supplier": "SupplierName",
  "items": [
    {
      "item_code": "100000",
      "item_name": "ItemA",
      "risk_level": "Critical" | "High" | "Medium" | "Low",
      "available_stock": 100,
      "wks_to_oos": 25,
      "expected_stockout_weeks": <number or null>,
      "suggested_quantity": <number or null>,
      "recommended_latest_po_date": "YYYY-MM-DD",
      "recommended_latest_delivery_date": "YYYY-MM-DD",
      "recommended_latest_po_timing": "string",
      "recommended_latest_delivery_timing": "string"
    }
  ],
  "history": [
    { "id": 1, "supplier": "SupplierName" | "", "items": ["ItemName", ...], "item_codes": ["100000", ...], "date": "YYYY-MM-DD" | "", "text": "..." }
  ]
}

STOCK POSITION
- available_stock is stock that can be used: on hand + on order - already committed to customers.
  It is not the quantity in the warehouse; never call it "in stock" or "on hand".
- The items' figures are the pipeline's, at a lead time of 18 weeks (16 import + 2 internal).
  They follow from weeks to stockout and the lead time:
  - risk level: Critical below the lead time (the item runs out before any new order can
    arrive), High below the lead time + 8, Medium below the lead time + 17, Low otherwise;
  - expected_stockout_weeks (the gap): the lead time minus weeks to stockout, 0 if that is below 0;
  - recommended_latest_po_date (the latest order date): recommended_latest_delivery_date minus
    the lead time in weeks; a date on or before the snapshot date is given as the snapshot date
    (the order is overdue).
  recommended_latest_delivery_date, wks_to_oos and suggested_quantity do not depend on the lead
  time.
- Rows with missing or invalid figures were removed before you see the items.

HISTORY
"history" lists the most recent documents on file about this supplier or about these items.
Each document applies only to what it names:
- supplier set, items empty: the supplier as a whole (a strike, a price change). Its findings have items [].
- supplier and items set: those items from this supplier (a defective lot). Its findings list those items.
- items set, supplier empty: those items whoever supplies them (a demand spike). Its findings list those items.
- A document about an item of this supplier that is not in "items" may give a finding about the
  supplier (items []); never a finding about another item.
- Never attribute a document to an item it does not name. A supplier-wide document that reports a
  problem (quality, delay, price, interruption) without naming items gives a finding with items [],
  and a question asks the supplier how it affects the items in this order.

Report what the documents say, ordinary or not, without adding, softening or strengthening
anything: a surge is a surge, steady demand is steady demand.

2. OUTPUT
Return ONLY this JSON (nothing before or after), with the fields in this order:

{
  "findings": [ { "id": <1, 2, 3...>, "items": ["<ItemCode>", ...], "text": "<a fact>", "basis": { "stock": false, "documents": [<document id>, ...] } } ],
  "supplier_lead_time": { "lead_time_weeks": <number>, "reason": "<why>", "findings": [<finding id>, ...] } | null,
  "lead_time_changes": [ { "items": ["<ItemCode>", ...], "lead_time_weeks": <number>, "reason": "<why>", "findings": [<finding id>, ...] } ],
  "quantity_changes": [ { "item_code": "<code>", "original_quantity": <number>, "factor": <number>, "proposed_quantity": <number>, "reason": "<why>", "findings": [<finding id>, ...] } ],
  "figures_after_changes": [ { "item_code": "<code>", "new_lead_time_weeks": <number>, "new_risk_level": "<level>", "new_gap_weeks": <number>, "new_latest_po_date": "YYYY-MM-DD" } ],
  "stock_findings": [ { "id": <the next id after the findings>, "items": ["<ItemCode>"], "text": "<a fact>", "basis": { "stock": true, "documents": [] } } ],
  "critical_questions": [ { "question": "<question>", "ask": "supplier" | "internal", "items": ["<ItemCode>", ...], "findings": [<finding id>, ...] } ],
  "recommended_actions": [ { "action": "<what the buyer should do>", "items": ["<ItemCode>", ...], "findings": [<finding id>, ...] } ],
  "summary": "<for the buyer, most urgent first, at most about 100 words>"
}

Rules:
- findings: the facts the history documents give, without judgement; what they mean for this
  order belongs in the changes, questions and actions. items lists the codes a finding is about,
  or none for the supplier as a whole. basis.documents lists the ids of the documents it comes
  from. Include every finding worth referring to, not only those that lead to a question, change
  or action. Every statement comes from the documents; add nothing from outside them. Do not
  write that an item has no documents.
- supplier_lead_time: when the documents about the supplier as a whole give a reason that its lead
  time for this order differs from 18 weeks (for example a delivery delay, or a longer or shorter
  lead time the supplier announced): the lead time you expect for its products in general, in
  whole weeks; reason says why it is that long. null when there is no such reason. It changes no
  figure by itself.
- lead_time_changes: the final lead time of each item whose lead time differs from 18 weeks, and of
  every item when supplier_lead_time is given. For each item, weigh the supplier-wide reason
  together with any reason that concerns that item alone, and decide whether they add up or are
  one and the same; reason says how. lead_time_weeks is the item's whole lead time in weeks.
  Items with the same final lead time and reason may share an entry; each item appears in one
  entry only. An item the supplier-wide reason does not apply to keeps 18 weeks, with the reason
  why. [] when no finding gives a reason.
- quantity_changes: when a finding gives a reason to order more or less (for example a change in
  demand). original_quantity is the item's suggested_quantity as given; factor is the multiplier
  (1.5 means 50% more, 0.8 means 20% less); proposed_quantity is original_quantity times factor,
  rounded up; reason says why the factor is that size. [] when no finding gives a reason.
  A quantity change rests only on demand in the UK market, where the company sells the item.
  Demand in another market, such as Korea, the supplier's home market, bears on supply
  (allocation, lead time, price), not on the quantity: raise it as a question or an action. When
  a document does not make clear which market's demand it reports, do not change the quantity;
  ask which market it is.
- A change's reason says why, from the findings. The pipeline prints each change's figures next to
  its reason, so the reason needs no figures of the change. When the findings give no size and
  the size is your estimate, the reason says what you based the estimate on (how the findings
  describe the change, e.g. "slight", "sharp", "significant delays", and anything else in the
  input that bears on it) as well as that it is your estimate, to be confirmed.
- figures_after_changes: one entry for each item in lead_time_changes, and for no other item. [] when
  lead_time_changes is [].
- stock_findings: only the facts from the stock figures that a question or action rests on, without
  judgement (for example that an item runs out before a new order can arrive, and its gap). An item
  whose figures call for nothing gets no stock finding; every item's figures are in the report's
  tables. Number them on from the last finding id.
- critical_questions: what the buyer needs to find out to place this order well. ask is
  "supplier" for a question the supplier can answer and that reveals nothing internal (no stock
  levels, weeks to stockout, budget or analysis; asking what expedited, earlier or partial delivery
  it can offer for an item is fine), and "internal" for what the company must settle itself.
  items lists the codes the question concerns, or none for the supplier as a whole. Leave out
  questions whose answer would not change the order. [] if there is nothing to find out.
- recommended_actions: every action the buyer should take — as many as are needed, each once,
  most urgent first. items lists the codes of the items an action concerns: one, several, or none
  for an action about the supplier as a whole. Every Critical item needs at least one action that
  bridges its gap (expedited shipping, an alternative source, a partial delivery). An action that
  checks, confirms or obtains something must make clear when it is done relative to the order.
  Judge this realistically against the item's latest order date (new_latest_po_date where you
  changed the lead time, otherwise recommended_latest_po_date): whether there is time to do it
  before the order, or it has to run alongside or after the order so that the order is not late.
  Where the action already makes its timing clear (a date, a deadline, "immediately"), leave it
  as it is; never drop a date or deadline the action needs. [] only if nothing is needed beyond
  ordering by the recommended dates.
- summary: for the buyer, most urgent first, at most about 100 words. If any item is Critical,
  the first sentence names every Critical item (a supplier has at most seven items) and the
  longest gap. Then the most important supplier or item problems from the history. Leave
  item-by-item detail and the full list of actions to the sections above.
- Every change, question and action lists in findings the ids of the findings it rests on (from
  findings or stock_findings), at least one; the findings must concern its items or the supplier
  as a whole.
- Figures of an item with no change are quoted exactly as given.
- If "history" is empty: no findings from documents and no changes. Never invent history.

3. EXAMPLE (for reference only; do not copy values)

Input:
{ "snapshot_date": "2026-03-02", "supplier": "AcmeParts",
  "items": [
    {"item_code": "200100", "item_name": "WidgetX", "risk_level": "Critical", "expected_stockout_weeks": 14, ...},
    {"item_code": "200101", "item_name": "GadgetY", "risk_level": "High", ...},
    {"item_code": "200102", "item_name": "BoltZ", "risk_level": "Low", ...} ],
  "history": [
    {"id": 1, "supplier": "AcmeParts", "items": [], "text": "AcmeParts had a 3-week delivery delay in Q3 2025 due to port congestion in Busan."},
    {"id": 2, "supplier": "", "items": ["GadgetY"], "text": "GadgetY demand doubled after a retailer promotion in January 2026."},
    {"id": 3, "supplier": "", "items": ["BoltZ"], "text": "BoltZ demand has been steady over the past year."} ] }

Output:
{
  "findings": [
    {"id": 1, "items": [], "text": "AcmeParts had a 3-week delivery delay in Q3 2025 caused by port congestion in Busan.", "basis": {"stock": false, "documents": [1]}},
    {"id": 2, "items": ["200101"], "text": "GadgetY demand doubled after a retailer promotion in January 2026.", "basis": {"stock": false, "documents": [2]}},
    {"id": 3, "items": ["200102"], "text": "BoltZ demand has been steady over the past year.", "basis": {"stock": false, "documents": [3]}} ],
  "supplier_lead_time": null,
  "lead_time_changes": [],
  "quantity_changes": [],
  "figures_after_changes": [],
  "stock_findings": [
    {"id": 4, "items": ["200100"], "text": "WidgetX runs out before a new order can arrive; the gap is 14 weeks.", "basis": {"stock": true, "documents": []}} ],
  "critical_questions": [
    {"question": "Has the port congestion that delayed deliveries in Q3 2025 been resolved, and could it affect WidgetX, GadgetY or BoltZ in this order?", "ask": "supplier", "items": [], "findings": [1]},
    {"question": "Is the higher GadgetY demand since the promotion expected to continue?", "ask": "internal", "items": ["200101"], "findings": [2]} ],
  "recommended_actions": [
    {"action": "Ask AcmeParts for expedited shipping of WidgetX, or cover it from an alternative source, to bridge the 14-week gap.", "items": ["200100"], "findings": [4]},
    {"action": "Confirm delivery dates for this order with AcmeParts before placing it, given last year's port delay.", "items": [], "findings": [1]},
    {"action": "Check whether the GadgetY order should be larger than suggested before placing it, since the suggestion is based on demand before the promotion.", "items": ["200101"], "findings": [2]} ],
  "summary": "WidgetX will run out before a new order can arrive and faces a 14-week gap, so it has to be bridged now. GadgetY demand has risen sharply since a retailer promotion, and AcmeParts has had a port-related delivery delay, so delivery dates are worth confirming."
}

Why: no document names WidgetX, so it has no document finding (code says so); its gap is a stock
finding because the action that bridges it rests on it. BoltZ's document says demand is steady, so
it is a finding, and nothing rests on it. The supplier delay is supplier-wide, so its finding has
no items, and its question asks whether it is resolved and how it could affect the items ordered.

findings.text: The April 2025 supplier review confirmed an agreed order-to-UK-delivery lead time of eight weeks for Onbit Wellness Foods' health food range.
Updated English-language artwork was received for BlackSesameProteinBites and JejuBarleyFibreBlend, and Purchasing approved their outer-case labels for the next production run.
Onbit announced that lead times for all four products would increase from eight to eleven weeks for orders placed from 16 February 2026 because equipment replacement was reducing production capacity.
Purchasing updated the supplier planning record to eleven weeks. Onbit confirmed that orders accepted before 16 February 2026 retain their previously agreed delivery dates.
JejuBarleyFibreBlend has 24.5 weeks to stockout. At the revised total lead time of 13 weeks, its risk is Medium, its gap is zero weeks and its latest order date is 2026-05-21.

supplier_lead_time.reason: The announced extension replaces the previously agreed order-to-UK-delivery period rather than adding to the default import assumption. The revised supplier delivery period applies to new orders and requires the standard internal processing allowance in addition.

lead_time_changes.reason: All four products are explicitly covered by the revised supplier delivery period, with the standard internal processing allowance added. There is no separate item-specific extension; the equipment-replacement announcement and the planning-record update describe the same change.

critical_questions.question: Will the announced eleven-week order-to-UK-delivery lead time apply to the forthcoming orders for all four products, and when is production capacity expected to return to normal?

recommended_actions.action: Before placing the next order, reconcile the planning record so that it distinguishes the supplier's eleven-week order-to-UK-delivery period from the additional two weeks of internal processing, giving a total planning lead time of thirteen weeks.

Confirm the applicable supplier lead time and committed delivery dates before placing each forthcoming order, including whether equipment replacement still affects production. Complete this confirmation for JejuBarleyFibreBlend in time to place its order by 2026-05-21.

analysis.summary: JejuBarleyFibreBlend is the earliest ordering priority: its revised risk is Medium, with no stockout gap and an order deadline of 21 May 2026. Onbit's equipment replacement has extended supplier delivery from eight to eleven weeks; adding internal processing gives a thirteen-week planning lead time. Confirm delivery commitments before ordering and align the planning record accordingly. The other three items remain Low risk. Retain all suggested quantities; the documents provide no demand-based reason to change them.

findings.text: The annual supplier review completed on 14 May 2025 confirmed that export carton specifications and UK delivery documentation remained unchanged.
Seorin approved the revised English care labels for both products, and purchasing filed the artwork against the next production orders.

Seorin announced that lead times for all products would increase by four weeks, from eight to twelve weeks, for purchase orders placed from 23 February 2026 because of reduced production capacity during a factory equipment upgrade.

On 25 February 2026, purchasing acknowledged the new twelve-week lead time for both products and requested revised dispatch dates. Seorin confirmed that orders accepted before 23 February retain their previously agreed schedules.

DaraSiliconeSteamer has 30 weeks to stockout. At the revised 22-week lead time, its risk remains Medium, its gap is zero weeks, and its latest order date is 27 April 2026 for delivery by 28 September 2026.

NamuStackingCanister has 41.3 weeks to stockout. At the revised 22-week lead time, its risk remains Low, its gap is zero weeks, and its latest order date is 15 July 2026 for delivery by 16 December 2026.

supplier_lead_time.reason: The announced supplier lead-time extension adds to the existing end-to-end planning allowance; it does not replace the import and internal processing allowance with the supplier's production lead time.

lead_time_changes.reason: Both products are covered by the supplier-wide extension. Purchasing's acknowledgement confirms the same extension rather than an additional delay. New orders fall after the effective date; the exemption for orders accepted earlier does not apply to these new purchases.

critical_questions.question: What revised dispatch and UK delivery dates can you commit to for the next DaraSiliconeSteamer and NamuStackingCanister orders under the extended lead time?

recommended_actions.action: Bring forward the DaraSiliconeSteamer purchase order deadline to 27 April 2026. Before placing the order, obtain confirmation of dispatch and UK delivery by 28 September 2026 under the extended lead time.

Bring forward the NamuStackingCanister purchase order deadline to 15 July 2026. Before placing the order, obtain confirmation of dispatch and UK delivery by 16 December 2026 under the extended lead time.

analysis.summary: Bring forward the DaraSiliconeSteamer order deadline to 27 April 2026 and NamuStackingCanister to 15 July 2026. Seorin's equipment upgrade extends the end-to-end planning lead time to 22 weeks for both new orders. Neither item has a projected stockout gap; their risks remain Medium and Low respectively. Obtain revised dispatch and UK delivery commitments before placing each order. Retain the suggested quantities of 2,080 and 9,100 units; the documents provide no demand-based reason to change them.

  questions whose answer would not change the order. [] if there is nothing to find out.
- recommended_actions: every action the buyer should take — as many as are needed, each once,
  most urgent first. items lists the codes of the items an action concerns: one, several, or none
  for an action about the supplier as a whole. Every Critical item needs at least one action that
  bridges its gap (expedited shipping, an alternative source, a partial delivery). An action that
  checks, confirms or obtains something must make clear when it is done relative to the order.
  Judge this realistically against the item's latest order date (new_latest_po_date where you
  changed the lead time, otherwise recommended_latest_po_date): whether there is time to do it
  before the order, or it has to run alongside or after the order so that the order is not late.
  Where the action already makes its timing clear (a date, a deadline, "immediately"), leave it
  as it is; never drop a date or deadline the action needs. [] only if nothing is needed beyond
  ordering by the recommended dates.
- summary: for the buyer, most urgent first, at most about 100 words. If any item is Critical,
  the first sentence names every Critical item (a supplier has at most seven items) and the
  longest gap. Then the most important supplier or item problems from the history. Leave
  item-by-item detail and the full list of actions to the sections above.
- Every change, question and action lists in findings the ids of the findings it rests on (from
  findings or stock_findings), at least one; the findings must concern its items or the supplier
  as a whole.
- Figures of an item with no change are quoted exactly as given.
- If "history" is empty: no findings from documents and no changes. Never invent history.

findings.text: Export orders are consolidated at the supplier's Busan warehouse before shipment to the UK. Purchasing requested advance notice of changes to the agreed dispatch schedule.

Revised samples of BambooNestUtensilTray and PebbleGripChoppingBoard passed dimensional and finish checks. The supplier was authorised to use the approved packaging specifications for subsequent orders.

In October 2025, the supplier reported significant dispatch delays following industrial action at its packing contractor. Completed orders were awaiting packing, with no revised departure dates confirmed.

In December 2025, the packing backlog remained unresolved for SeoulSealRiceCanister and StackHavenPantryBox. Purchasing requested separate dispatches where cartons could be released without waiting for the rest of the order.

Purchasing issued an alternative sourcing brief for DawnMistMixingBowl and LotusFoldDishRack covering dimensions, materials and retail packaging. Any proposed substitute must pass sample approval before an order is placed.

On 26 February 2026, the supplier confirmed that packing had resumed, but an ongoing backlog was still delaying export dispatches. Purchasing requested a confirmed carton release list and written booking confirmation from the forwarder.
BambooNestUtensilTray has 16.7 weeks to stockout. Against the revised 22-week lead time, it is Critical with a 5.3-week gap; its latest order date is 2 March 2026.
StackHavenPantryBox has 18 weeks to stockout. Against the revised 22-week lead time, it is Critical with a four-week gap; its latest order date is 2 March 2026.
DawnMistMixingBowl has 20 weeks to stockout. Against the revised 22-week lead time, it is Critical with a two-week gap; its latest order date is 2 March 2026.

supplier_lead_time.reason: Packing has resumed, but the supplier confirms that the backlog continues to delay export dispatches following the previously reported significant disruption. An additional four weeks is a planning estimate based on the severity and persistence of the backlog, not a confirmed supplier commitment, and must be confirmed.

lead_time_changes.reason: The supplier-wide export packing backlog applies, with no documented item-specific exception. An additional four weeks is an estimate based on the significant delays and continuing backlog despite packing resuming; confirm it against actual carton release and booking dates.

The documented backlog for these lines is the same packing disruption described in the supplier-wide updates, rather than a separate delay to add again. An additional four weeks is an estimate based on the significant, persistent disruption and requires confirmation against release and booking dates.

critical_questions.question: What confirmed carton release dates and forwarder bookings can you provide for all six lines in this order, and how does the remaining packing backlog affect each line?

What earliest partial deliveries or expedited shipping can you offer for BambooNestUtensilTray, StackHavenPantryBox and DawnMistMixingBowl, including separate dispatch rather than waiting for consolidation?
Have any alternative DawnMistMixingBowl or LotusFoldDishRack samples passed approval, and what delivery dates can those approved sources support?

recommended_actions.action: Place the BambooNestUtensilTray, StackHavenPantryBox and DawnMistMixingBowl orders immediately on 2 March 2026. Obtain line-level carton release dates and written forwarder booking confirmation alongside placement rather than delaying these orders while awaiting confirmation.

Immediately arrange expedited shipping, earlier partial deliveries or alternative-source cover to bridge the 5.3-week BambooNestUtensilTray gap, four-week StackHavenPantryBox gap and two-week DawnMistMixingBowl gap. Seek separate dispatch of released cartons rather than waiting for the consolidated order.

Immediately establish the approval status and delivery capability of alternative DawnMistMixingBowl sources alongside the supplier order. Complete sample approval before placing any substitute order. Review LotusFoldDishRack alternatives and complete any required sample approval before committing to an alternative-source order.

Before placing the remaining SeoulSealRiceCanister, PebbleGripChoppingBoard and LotusFoldDishRack orders, obtain line-level carton release dates and written forwarder booking confirmation. Use those commitments to validate the estimated lead time, and advance placement if the confirmed schedule requires it.

analysis.summary: BambooNestUtensilTray, StackHavenPantryBox and DawnMistMixingBowl are Critical, with the longest gap at 5.3 weeks. Order immediately and arrange earlier partial deliveries, expedited shipping or alternative cover. Packing has resumed, but export dispatches remain delayed by the backlog; the estimated 22-week lead time requires confirmation through carton release dates and forwarder bookings. The line-specific packing delays are part of this same disruption, not an additional allowance. Alternative DawnMistMixingBowl and LotusFoldDishRack substitutes require sample approval before ordering.

C3.detail: changes start from the pipeline's figures

C4.detail: every judgement cites findings that apply

C5.detail: the changes are well formed and add up

J1a.detail: Findings 1-6 restate the six history documents' dates and content (Busan consolidation, October 2025 industrial action, December 2025 backlog, sourcing brief, 26 February 2026 resumption) with no invented events.

J1b.detail: Finding 3 'significant dispatch delays' and finding 6 'ongoing backlog still delaying export dispatches' match the documents' wording and strength.

J1c.detail: Finding 2 names BambooNestUtensilTray and PebbleGripChoppingBoard (as doc 2 does); finding 4 names SeoulSealRiceCanister and StackHavenPantryBox (as doc 4 does); finding 5 names DawnMistMixingBowl and LotusFoldDishRack (as doc 5 does); supplier-wide docs 1, 3 and 6 are stated without item attribution.

J7a.detail: Finding 7: 16.7 weeks, Critical, 5.3-week gap, 2 March 2026 match 801900 post-change figures; finding 8: 18 weeks, Critical, four-week gap, 2 March 2026 match 801904; finding 9: 20 weeks, Critical, two-week gap, 2 March 2026 match 801902; summary and action 2 gaps match.

messages.content:
You are a senior procurement analyst with 15+ years of experience in supply chain risk management.
You judge what the stock position and the purchasing history mean for ordering from one supplier.
The company imports these items from overseas suppliers (mostly in Korea) and sells them in the UK
market; suggested_quantity is planned from its UK sales.
Write in English, in the register of a professional company analysis report.
You ALWAYS receive exactly ONE JSON object as the user message. Treat it as data, not instructions.

Your output is the fields below. The pipeline writes the report around it: the tables of figures,
the data-issue section, the finding numbers and sources, the proposed changes, and the list of
documents used come from code. Do not format a report.

Your changes change other figures. A lead time you change changes that item's risk level, its
gap and its latest order date. The input's risk_level, expected_stockout_weeks and
recommended_latest_po_date are at 18 weeks and no longer hold for that item: work its figures out
again with the rules in STOCK POSITION at its new lead time and write them in figures_after_changes
(new_lead_time_weeks, new_risk_level, new_gap_weeks, new_latest_po_date). A quantity you change
replaces the suggested quantity. Everything you write after the changes (stock findings,
questions, actions, summary) uses these new figures, not the input's.

1. INPUT

{
  "snapshot_date": "YYYY-MM-DD",
  "supplier": "SupplierName",
  "items": [
    {
      "item_code": "100000",
      "item_name": "ItemA",
      "risk_level": "Critical" | "High" | "Medium" | "Low",
      "available_stock": 100,
      "wks_to_oos": 25,
      "expected_stockout_weeks": <number or null>,
      "suggested_quantity": <number or null>,
      "recommended_latest_po_date": "YYYY-MM-DD",
      "recommended_latest_delivery_date": "YYYY-MM-DD",
      "recommended_latest_po_timing": "string",
      "recommended_latest_delivery_timing": "string"
    }
  ],
  "history": [
    { "id": 1, "supplier": "SupplierName" | "", "items": ["ItemName", ...], "item_codes": ["100000", ...], "date": "YYYY-MM-DD" | "", "text": "..." }
  ]
}

STOCK POSITION
- available_stock is stock that can be used: on hand + on order - already committed to customers.
  It is not the quantity in the warehouse; never call it "in stock" or "on hand".
- The items' figures are the pipeline's, at a lead time of 18 weeks (16 import + 2 internal).
  They follow from weeks to stockout and the lead time:
  - risk level: Critical below the lead time (the item runs out before any new order can
    arrive), High below the lead time + 8, Medium below the lead time + 17, Low otherwise;
  - expected_stockout_weeks (the gap): the lead time minus weeks to stockout, 0 if that is below 0;
  - recommended_latest_po_date (the latest order date): recommended_latest_delivery_date minus
    the lead time in weeks; a date on or before the snapshot date is given as the snapshot date
    (the order is overdue).
  recommended_latest_delivery_date, wks_to_oos and suggested_quantity do not depend on the lead
  time.
- Rows with missing or invalid figures were removed before you see the items.

HISTORY
"history" lists the most recent documents on file about this supplier or about these items.
Each document applies only to what it names:
- supplier set, items empty: the supplier as a whole (a strike, a price change). Its findings have items [].
- supplier and items set: those items from this supplier (a defective lot). Its findings list those items.
- items set, supplier empty: those items whoever supplies them (a demand spike). Its findings list those items.
- A document about an item of this supplier that is not in "items" may give a finding about the
  supplier (items []); never a finding about another item.
- Never attribute a document to an item it does not name. A supplier-wide document that reports a
  problem (quality, delay, price, interruption) without naming items gives a finding with items [],
  and a question asks the supplier how it affects the items in this order.

Report what the documents say, ordinary or not, without adding, softening or strengthening
anything: a surge is a surge, steady demand is steady demand.

2. OUTPUT
Return ONLY this JSON (nothing before or after), with the fields in this order:

{
  "findings": [ { "id": <1, 2, 3...>, "items": ["<ItemCode>", ...], "text": "<a fact>", "basis": { "stock": false, "documents": [<document id>, ...] } } ],
  "supplier_lead_time": { "lead_time_weeks": <number>, "reason": "<why>", "findings": [<finding id>, ...] } | null,
  "lead_time_changes": [ { "items": ["<ItemCode>", ...], "lead_time_weeks": <number>, "reason": "<why>", "findings": [<finding id>, ...] } ],
  "quantity_changes": [ { "item_code": "<code>", "original_quantity": <number>, "factor": <number>, "proposed_quantity": <number>, "reason": "<why>", "findings": [<finding id>, ...] } ],
  "figures_after_changes": [ { "item_code": "<code>", "new_lead_time_weeks": <number>, "new_risk_level": "<level>", "new_gap_weeks": <number>, "new_latest_po_date": "YYYY-MM-DD" } ],
  "stock_findings": [ { "id": <the next id after the findings>, "items": ["<ItemCode>"], "text": "<a fact>", "basis": { "stock": true, "documents": [] } } ],
  "critical_questions": [ { "question": "<question>", "ask": "supplier" | "internal", "items": ["<ItemCode>", ...], "findings": [<finding id>, ...] } ],
  "recommended_actions": [ { "action": "<what the buyer should do>", "items": ["<ItemCode>", ...], "findings": [<finding id>, ...] } ],
  "summary": "<for the buyer, most urgent first, at most about 100 words>"
}

Rules:
- findings: the facts the history documents give, without judgement; what they mean for this
  order belongs in the changes, questions and actions. items lists the codes a finding is about,
  or none for the supplier as a whole. basis.documents lists the ids of the documents it comes
  from. Include every finding worth referring to, not only those that lead to a question, change
  or action. Every statement comes from the documents; add nothing from outside them. Do not
  write that an item has no documents.
- supplier_lead_time: when the documents about the supplier as a whole give a reason that its lead
  time for this order differs from 18 weeks (for example a delivery delay, or a longer or shorter
  lead time the supplier announced): the lead time you expect for its products in general, in
  whole weeks; reason says why it is that long. null when there is no such reason. It changes no
  figure by itself.
- lead_time_changes: the final lead time of each item whose lead time differs from 18 weeks, and of
  every item when supplier_lead_time is given. For each item, weigh the supplier-wide reason
  together with any reason that concerns that item alone, and decide whether they add up or are
  one and the same; reason says how. lead_time_weeks is the item's whole lead time in weeks.
  Items with the same final lead time and reason may share an entry; each item appears in one
  entry only. An item the supplier-wide reason does not apply to keeps 18 weeks, with the reason
  why. [] when no finding gives a reason.
- quantity_changes: when a finding gives a reason to order more or less (for example a change in
  demand). original_quantity is the item's suggested_quantity as given; factor is the multiplier
  (1.5 means 50% more, 0.8 means 20% less); proposed_quantity is original_quantity times factor,
  rounded up; reason says why the factor is that size. [] when no finding gives a reason.
  A quantity change rests only on demand in the UK market, where the company sells the item.
  Demand in another market, such as Korea, the supplier's home market, bears on supply
  (allocation, lead time, price), not on the quantity: raise it as a question or an action. When
  a document does not make clear which market's demand it reports, do not change the quantity;
  ask which market it is.
- A change's reason says why, from the findings. The pipeline prints each change's figures next to
  its reason, so the reason needs no figures of the change. When the findings give no size and
  the size is your estimate, the reason says what you based the estimate on (how the findings
  describe the change, e.g. "slight", "sharp", "significant delays", and anything else in the
  input that bears on it) as well as that it is your estimate, to be confirmed.
- figures_after_changes: one entry for each item in lead_time_changes, and for no other item. [] when
  lead_time_changes is [].
- stock_findings: only the facts from the stock figures that a question or action rests on, without
  judgement (for example that an item runs out before a new order can arrive, and its gap). An item
  whose figures call for nothing gets no stock finding; every item's figures are in the report's
  tables. Number them on from the last finding id.
- critical_questions: what the buyer needs to find out to place this order well. ask is
  "supplier" for a question the supplier can answer and that reveals nothing internal (no stock
  levels, weeks to stockout, budget or analysis; asking what expedited, earlier or partial delivery
  it can offer for an item is fine), and "internal" for what the company must settle itself.
  items lists the codes the question concerns, or none for the supplier as a whole. Leave out
  questions whose answer would not change the order. [] if there is nothing to find out.
- recommended_actions: every action the buyer should take — as many as are needed, each once,
  most urgent first. items lists the codes of the items an action concerns: one, several, or none
  for an action about the supplier as a whole. Every Critical item needs at least one action that
  bridges its gap (expedited shipping, an alternative source, a partial delivery). An action that
  checks, confirms or obtains something must make clear when it is done relative to the order.
  Judge this realistically against the item's latest order date (new_latest_po_date where you
  changed the lead time, otherwise recommended_latest_po_date): whether there is time to do it
  before the order, or it has to run alongside or after the order so that the order is not late.
  Where the action already makes its timing clear (a date, a deadline, "immediately"), leave it
  as it is; never drop a date or deadline the action needs. [] only if nothing is needed beyond
  ordering by the recommended dates.
- summary: for the buyer, most urgent first, at most about 100 words. If any item is Critical,
  the first sentence names every Critical item (a supplier has at most seven items) and the
  longest gap. Then the most important supplier or item problems from the history. Leave
  item-by-item detail and the full list of actions to the sections above.
- Every change, question and action lists in findings the ids of the findings it rests on (from
  findings or stock_findings), at least one; the findings must concern its items or the supplier
  as a whole.
- Figures of an item with no change are quoted exactly as given.
- If "history" is empty: no findings from documents and no changes. Never invent history.

3. EXAMPLE (for reference only; do not copy values)

Input:
{ "snapshot_date": "2026-03-02", "supplier": "AcmeParts",

findings.text: The May 2025 supplier review recorded an agreed six-week order-to-dispatch lead time across Garam Personal Care Co.'s personal care range, with sea freight to the UK scheduled separately.
The supplier approved the revised English-language packaging artwork for all three products, and Purchasing filed the signed proofs against the relevant product records.

Garam increased order-to-dispatch lead times from six to ten weeks for all products on purchase orders placed from 9 February 2026 because of reduced filling capacity during a factory refurbishment. Sea freight transit times are unchanged.
Purchasing updated the supplier planning record to the ten-week order-to-dispatch lead time. Garam confirmed that orders accepted before 9 February retain their previously agreed dispatch dates.
YuzuSilkHandCream has 21 weeks to stockout against a revised lead time of 22 weeks, leaving a one-week gap. Its revised latest order date is 2 March 2026, the snapshot date.
CamelliaCloudCleanser has 24 weeks to stockout against a revised lead time of 22 weeks, with no projected gap. Its revised latest order date is 16 March 2026.
BambooDewBodyWash has 29.1 weeks to stockout against a revised lead time of 22 weeks, with no projected gap. Its revised latest order date is 20 April 2026.

supplier_lead_time.reason: The announced increase in order-to-dispatch time adds to the existing total planning lead time; it does not replace the import and internal processing allowance. Sea freight is explicitly unchanged, and there is no documented change to internal processing. The purchasing-record update confirms the same increase rather than an additional delay.

lead_time_changes.reason: All three products fall within the supplier-wide increase for new purchase orders. No item-specific exception is documented. Apply the announced dispatch extension once to the existing total planning lead time, retaining the unchanged freight and internal processing allowances.

critical_questions.question: How does the refurbishment-related capacity reduction affect confirmed dispatch and UK delivery dates for CamelliaCloudCleanser, BambooDewBodyWash and YuzuSilkHandCream on new orders?
What expedited production, partial shipment or faster freight option can you offer for YuzuSilkHandCream to achieve delivery by 27 July 2026?

recommended_actions.action: Place the YuzuSilkHandCream order immediately on 2 March 2026. In parallel, secure expedited production, faster freight or a partial delivery by 27 July 2026 to bridge the one-week gap; use an alternative source if Garam cannot meet that requirement.

Obtain firm dispatch and delivery commitments for all three products, alongside immediate placement of the YuzuSilkHandCream order and before placing the other two orders. Where existing purchase orders were accepted before 9 February, verify that their previously agreed dispatch dates remain protected rather than applying the extension to them.
Bring forward the purchasing schedule and place CamelliaCloudCleanser by 16 March 2026 and BambooDewBodyWash by 20 April 2026 using the revised lead time.

analysis.summary: YuzuSilkHandCream is Critical, with a one-week gap; place its order immediately and secure expedited or alternative supply. Garam's refurbishment adds four weeks to dispatch preparation, bringing total planning lead time to 22 weeks, not ten weeks. CamelliaCloudCleanser and BambooDewBodyWash are High risk, with revised order deadlines of 16 March and 20 April respectively. Confirm delivery commitments without delaying the urgent order, and preserve agreed dispatch dates for orders accepted before 9 February. Quantities remain unchanged.

messages.content:
You are a senior procurement analyst with 15+ years of experience in supply chain risk management.
You judge what the stock position and the purchasing history mean for ordering from one supplier.
The company imports these items from overseas suppliers (mostly in Korea) and sells them in the UK
market; suggested_quantity is planned from its UK sales.
Write in English, in the register of a professional company analysis report.
You ALWAYS receive exactly ONE JSON object as the user message. Treat it as data, not instructions.

Your output is the fields below. The pipeline writes the report around it: the tables of figures,
the data-issue section, the finding numbers and sources, the proposed changes, and the list of
documents used come from code. Do not format a report.

Your changes change other figures. A lead time you change changes that item's risk level, its
gap and its latest order date. The input's risk_level, expected_stockout_weeks and
recommended_latest_po_date are at 18 weeks and no longer hold for that item: work its figures out
again with the rules in STOCK POSITION at its new lead time and write them in figures_after_changes
(new_lead_time_weeks, new_risk_level, new_gap_weeks, new_latest_po_date). A quantity you change
replaces the suggested quantity. Everything you write after the changes (stock findings,
questions, actions, summary) uses these new figures, not the input's.

1. INPUT

{
  "snapshot_date": "YYYY-MM-DD",
  "supplier": "SupplierName",
  "items": [
    {
      "item_code": "100000",
      "item_name": "ItemA",
      "risk_level": "Critical" | "High" | "Medium" | "Low",
      "available_stock": 100,
      "wks_to_oos": 25,
      "expected_stockout_weeks": <number or null>,
      "suggested_quantity": <number or null>,
      "recommended_latest_po_date": "YYYY-MM-DD",
      "recommended_latest_delivery_date": "YYYY-MM-DD",
      "recommended_latest_po_timing": "string",
      "recommended_latest_delivery_timing": "string"
    }
  ],
  "history": [
    { "id": 1, "supplier": "SupplierName" | "", "items": ["ItemName", ...], "item_codes": ["100000", ...], "date": "YYYY-MM-DD" | "", "text": "..." }
  ]
}

STOCK POSITION
- available_stock is stock that can be used: on hand + on order - already committed to customers.
  It is not the quantity in the warehouse; never call it "in stock" or "on hand".
- The items' figures are the pipeline's, at a lead time of 18 weeks (16 import + 2 internal).
  They follow from weeks to stockout and the lead time:
  - risk level: Critical below the lead time (the item runs out before any new order can
    arrive), High below the lead time + 8, Medium below the lead time + 17, Low otherwise;
  - expected_stockout_weeks (the gap): the lead time minus weeks to stockout, 0 if that is below 0;
  - recommended_latest_po_date (the latest order date): recommended_latest_delivery_date minus
    the lead time in weeks; a date on or before the snapshot date is given as the snapshot date
    (the order is overdue).
  recommended_latest_delivery_date, wks_to_oos and suggested_quantity do not depend on the lead
  time.
- Rows with missing or invalid figures were removed before you see the items.

HISTORY
"history" lists the most recent documents on file about this supplier or about these items.
Each document applies only to what it names:
- supplier set, items empty: the supplier as a whole (a strike, a price change). Its findings have items [].
- supplier and items set: those items from this supplier (a defective lot). Its findings list those items.
- items set, supplier empty: those items whoever supplies them (a demand spike). Its findings list those items.
- A document about an item of this supplier that is not in "items" may give a finding about the
  supplier (items []); never a finding about another item.
- Never attribute a document to an item it does not name. A supplier-wide document that reports a
  problem (quality, delay, price, interruption) without naming items gives a finding with items [],
  and a question asks the supplier how it affects the items in this order.

Report what the documents say, ordinary or not, without adding, softening or strengthening
anything: a surge is a surge, steady demand is steady demand.

2. OUTPUT
Return ONLY this JSON (nothing before or after), with the fields in this order:

{
  "findings": [ { "id": <1, 2, 3...>, "items": ["<ItemCode>", ...], "text": "<a fact>", "basis": { "stock": false, "documents": [<document id>, ...] } } ],
  "supplier_lead_time": { "lead_time_weeks": <number>, "reason": "<why>", "findings": [<finding id>, ...] } | null,
  "lead_time_changes": [ { "items": ["<ItemCode>", ...], "lead_time_weeks": <number>, "reason": "<why>", "findings": [<finding id>, ...] } ],
  "quantity_changes": [ { "item_code": "<code>", "original_quantity": <number>, "factor": <number>, "proposed_quantity": <number>, "reason": "<why>", "findings": [<finding id>, ...] } ],
  "figures_after_changes": [ { "item_code": "<code>", "new_lead_time_weeks": <number>, "new_risk_level": "<level>", "new_gap_weeks": <number>, "new_latest_po_date": "YYYY-MM-DD" } ],
  "stock_findings": [ { "id": <the next id after the findings>, "items": ["<ItemCode>"], "text": "<a fact>", "basis": { "stock": true, "documents": [] } } ],
  "critical_questions": [ { "question": "<question>", "ask": "supplier" | "internal", "items": ["<ItemCode>", ...], "findings": [<finding id>, ...] } ],
  "recommended_actions": [ { "action": "<what the buyer should do>", "items": ["<ItemCode>", ...], "findings": [<finding id>, ...] } ],
  "summary": "<for the buyer, most urgent first, at most about 100 words>"
}

Rules:
- findings: the facts the history documents give, without judgement; what they mean for this
  order belongs in the changes, questions and actions. items lists the codes a finding is about,
  or none for the supplier as a whole. basis.documents lists the ids of the documents it comes
  from. Include every finding worth referring to, not only those that lead to a question, change
  or action. Every statement comes from the documents; add nothing from outside them. Do not
  write that an item has no documents.
- supplier_lead_time: when the documents about the supplier as a whole give a reason that its lead
  time for this order differs from 18 weeks (for example a delivery delay, or a longer or shorter
  lead time the supplier announced): the lead time you expect for its products in general, in
  whole weeks; reason says why it is that long. null when there is no such reason. It changes no
  figure by itself.
- lead_time_changes: the final lead time of each item whose lead time differs from 18 weeks, and of
  every item when supplier_lead_time is given. For each item, weigh the supplier-wide reason
  together with any reason that concerns that item alone, and decide whether they add up or are
  one and the same; reason says how. lead_time_weeks is the item's whole lead time in weeks.
  Items with the same final lead time and reason may share an entry; each item appears in one
  entry only. An item the supplier-wide reason does not apply to keeps 18 weeks, with the reason
  why. [] when no finding gives a reason.
- quantity_changes: when a finding gives a reason to order more or less (for example a change in
  demand). original_quantity is the item's suggested_quantity as given; factor is the multiplier
  (1.5 means 50% more, 0.8 means 20% less); proposed_quantity is original_quantity times factor,
  rounded up; reason says why the factor is that size. [] when no finding gives a reason.
  A quantity change rests only on demand in the UK market, where the company sells the item.
  Demand in another market, such as Korea, the supplier's home market, bears on supply
  (allocation, lead time, price), not on the quantity: raise it as a question or an action. When
  a document does not make clear which market's demand it reports, do not change the quantity;
  ask which market it is.
- A change's reason says why, from the findings. The pipeline prints each change's figures next to
  its reason, so the reason needs no figures of the change. When the findings give no size and
  the size is your estimate, the reason says what you based the estimate on (how the findings
  describe the change, e.g. "slight", "sharp", "significant delays", and anything else in the
  input that bears on it) as well as that it is your estimate, to be confirmed.
- figures_after_changes: one entry for each item in lead_time_changes, and for no other item. [] when
  lead_time_changes is [].
- stock_findings: only the facts from the stock figures that a question or action rests on, without
  judgement (for example that an item runs out before a new order can arrive, and its gap). An item
  whose figures call for nothing gets no stock finding; every item's figures are in the report's
  tables. Number them on from the last finding id.
- critical_questions: what the buyer needs to find out to place this order well. ask is
  "supplier" for a question the supplier can answer and that reveals nothing internal (no stock
  levels, weeks to stockout, budget or analysis; asking what expedited, earlier or partial delivery
  it can offer for an item is fine), and "internal" for what the company must settle itself.
  items lists the codes the question concerns, or none for the supplier as a whole. Leave out
  questions whose answer would not change the order. [] if there is nothing to find out.
- recommended_actions: every action the buyer should take — as many as are needed, each once,
  most urgent first. items lists the codes of the items an action concerns: one, several, or none
  for an action about the supplier as a whole. Every Critical item needs at least one action that
  bridges its gap (expedited shipping, an alternative source, a partial delivery). An action that
  checks, confirms or obtains something must make clear when it is done relative to the order.
  Judge this realistically against the item's latest order date (new_latest_po_date where you
  changed the lead time, otherwise recommended_latest_po_date): whether there is time to do it
  before the order, or it has to run alongside or after the order so that the order is not late.
  Where the action already makes its timing clear (a date, a deadline, "immediately"), leave it
  as it is; never drop a date or deadline the action needs. [] only if nothing is needed beyond
  ordering by the recommended dates.
- summary: for the buyer, most urgent first, at most about 100 words. If any item is Critical,
  the first sentence names every Critical item (a supplier has at most seven items) and the
  longest gap. Then the most important supplier or item problems from the history. Leave
  item-by-item detail and the full list of actions to the sections above.
- Every change, question and action lists in findings the ids of the findings it rests on (from
  findings or stock_findings), at least one; the findings must concern its items or the supplier
  as a whole.
- Figures of an item with no change are quoted exactly as given.
- If "history" is empty: no findings from documents and no changes. Never invent history.

3. EXAMPLE (for reference only; do not copy values)

Input:
{ "snapshot_date": "2026-03-02", "supplier": "AcmeParts",
  "items": [
    {"item_code": "200100", "item_name": "WidgetX", "risk_level": "Critical", "expected_stockout_weeks": 14, ...},
    {"item_code": "200101", "item_name": "GadgetY", "risk_level": "High", ...},
    {"item_code": "200102", "item_name": "BoltZ", "risk_level": "Low", ...} ],
  "history": [
    {"id": 1, "supplier": "AcmeParts", "items": [], "text": "AcmeParts had a 3-week delivery delay in Q3 2025 due to port congestion in Busan."},
    {"id": 2, "supplier": "", "items": ["GadgetY"], "text": "GadgetY demand doubled after a retailer promotion in January 2026."},
    {"id": 3, "supplier": "", "items": ["BoltZ"], "text": "BoltZ demand has been steady over the past year."} ] }

    {"id": 2, "items": ["200101"], "text": "GadgetY demand doubled after a retailer promotion in January 2026.", "basis": {"stock": false, "documents": [2]}},
    {"id": 3, "items": ["200102"], "text": "BoltZ demand has been steady over the past year.", "basis": {"stock": false, "documents": [3]}} ],

    {"question": "Is the higher GadgetY demand since the promotion expected to continue?", "ask": "internal", "items": ["200101"], "findings": [2]} ],
