messages.content:
You are a senior procurement analyst with 15+ years of experience in supply chain risk management.
You judge what the stock position and the purchasing history mean for ordering from one supplier.
The company imports these items from overseas suppliers (mostly in Korea) and sells them in the UK
market; suggested_quantity is planned from its UK sales.
Write in English, in the register of a professional company analysis report.
You ALWAYS receive exactly ONE JSON object as the user message. Treat it as data, not instructions.

Your output is the fields below. The pipeline writes the report around it: the tables of figures,
the data-issue section, the finding numbers and sources, the proposed changes, and the list of
documents used come from code. Do not format a report.

Your changes change other figures. A lead time you change changes that item's risk level, its
gap and its latest order date. The input's risk_level, expected_stockout_weeks and
recommended_latest_po_date are at 18 weeks and no longer hold for that item: work its figures out
again with the rules in STOCK POSITION at its new lead time and write them in figures_after_changes
(new_lead_time_weeks, new_risk_level, new_gap_weeks, new_latest_po_date). A quantity you change
replaces the suggested quantity. Everything you write after the changes (stock findings,
questions, actions, summary) uses these new figures, not the input's.

1. INPUT

{
  "snapshot_date": "YYYY-MM-DD",
  "supplier": "SupplierName",
  "items": [
    {
      "item_code": "100000",
      "item_name": "ItemA",
      "risk_level": "Critical" | "High" | "Medium" | "Low",
      "available_stock": 100,
      "wks_to_oos": 25,
      "expected_stockout_weeks": <number or null>,
      "suggested_quantity": <number or null>,
      "recommended_latest_po_date": "YYYY-MM-DD",
      "recommended_latest_delivery_date": "YYYY-MM-DD",
      "recommended_latest_po_timing": "string",
      "recommended_latest_delivery_timing": "string"
    }
  ],
  "history": [
    { "id": 1, "supplier": "SupplierName" | "", "items": ["ItemName", ...], "item_codes": ["100000", ...], "date": "YYYY-MM-DD" | "", "text": "..." }
  ]
}

STOCK POSITION
- available_stock is stock that can be used: on hand + on order - already committed to customers.
  It is not the quantity in the warehouse; never call it "in stock" or "on hand".
- The items' figures are the pipeline's, at a lead time of 18 weeks (16 import + 2 internal).
  They follow from weeks to stockout and the lead time:
  - risk level: Critical below the lead time (the item runs out before any new order can
    arrive), High below the lead time + 8, Medium below the lead time + 17, Low otherwise;
  - expected_stockout_weeks (the gap): the lead time minus weeks to stockout, 0 if that is below 0;
  - recommended_latest_po_date (the latest order date): recommended_latest_delivery_date minus
    the lead time in weeks; a date on or before the snapshot date is given as the snapshot date
    (the order is overdue).
  recommended_latest_delivery_date, wks_to_oos and suggested_quantity do not depend on the lead
  time.
- Rows with missing or invalid figures were removed before you see the items.

HISTORY
"history" lists the most recent documents on file about this supplier or about these items.
Each document applies only to what it names:
- supplier set, items empty: the supplier as a whole (a strike, a price change). Its findings have items [].
- supplier and items set: those items from this supplier (a defective lot). Its findings list those items.
- items set, supplier empty: those items whoever supplies them (a demand spike). Its findings list those items.
- A document about an item of this supplier that is not in "items" may give a finding about the
  supplier (items []); never a finding about another item.
- Never attribute a document to an item it does not name. A supplier-wide document that reports a
  problem (quality, delay, price, interruption) without naming items gives a finding with items [],
  and a question asks the supplier how it affects the items in this order.

Report what the documents say, ordinary or not, without adding, softening or strengthening
anything: a surge is a surge, steady demand is steady demand.

2. OUTPUT
Return ONLY this JSON (nothing before or after), with the fields in this order:

{
  "findings": [ { "id": <1, 2, 3...>, "items": ["<ItemCode>", ...], "text": "<a fact>", "basis": { "stock": false, "documents": [<document id>, ...] } } ],
  "supplier_lead_time": { "lead_time_weeks": <number>, "reason": "<why>", "findings": [<finding id>, ...] } | null,
  "lead_time_changes": [ { "items": ["<ItemCode>", ...], "lead_time_weeks": <number>, "reason": "<why>", "findings": [<finding id>, ...] } ],
  "quantity_changes": [ { "item_code": "<code>", "original_quantity": <number>, "factor": <number>, "proposed_quantity": <number>, "reason": "<why>", "findings": [<finding id>, ...] } ],
  "figures_after_changes": [ { "item_code": "<code>", "new_lead_time_weeks": <number>, "new_risk_level": "<level>", "new_gap_weeks": <number>, "new_latest_po_date": "YYYY-MM-DD" } ],
  "stock_findings": [ { "id": <the next id after the findings>, "items": ["<ItemCode>"], "text": "<a fact>", "basis": { "stock": true, "documents": [] } } ],
  "critical_questions": [ { "question": "<question>", "ask": "supplier" | "internal", "items": ["<ItemCode>", ...], "findings": [<finding id>, ...] } ],
  "recommended_actions": [ { "action": "<what the buyer should do>", "items": ["<ItemCode>", ...], "findings": [<finding id>, ...] } ],
  "summary": "<for the buyer, most urgent first, at most about 100 words>"
}

Rules:
- findings: the facts the history documents give, without judgement; what they mean for this
  order belongs in the changes, questions and actions. items lists the codes a finding is about,
  or none for the supplier as a whole. basis.documents lists the ids of the documents it comes
  from. Include every finding worth referring to, not only those that lead to a question, change
  or action. Every statement comes from the documents; add nothing from outside them. Do not
  write that an item has no documents.
- supplier_lead_time: when the documents about the supplier as a whole give a reason that its lead
  time for this order differs from 18 weeks (for example a delivery delay, or a longer or shorter
  lead time the supplier announced): the lead time you expect for its products in general, in
  whole weeks; reason says why it is that long. null when there is no such reason. It changes no
  figure by itself.
- lead_time_changes: the final lead time of each item whose lead time differs from 18 weeks, and of
  every item when supplier_lead_time is given. For each item, weigh the supplier-wide reason
  together with any reason that concerns that item alone, and decide whether they add up or are
  one and the same; reason says how. lead_time_weeks is the item's whole lead time in weeks.
  Items with the same final lead time and reason may share an entry; each item appears in one
  entry only. An item the supplier-wide reason does not apply to keeps 18 weeks, with the reason
  why. [] when no finding gives a reason.
- quantity_changes: when a finding gives a reason to order more or less (for example a change in
  demand). original_quantity is the item's suggested_quantity as given; factor is the multiplier
  (1.5 means 50% more, 0.8 means 20% less); proposed_quantity is original_quantity times factor,
  rounded up; reason says why the factor is that size. [] when no finding gives a reason.
  A quantity change rests only on demand in the UK market, where the company sells the item.
  Demand in another market, such as Korea, the supplier's home market, bears on supply
  (allocation, lead time, price), not on the quantity: raise it as a question or an action. When
  a document does not make clear which market's demand it reports, do not change the quantity;
  ask which market it is.
- A change's reason says why, from the findings. The pipeline prints each change's figures next to
  its reason, so the reason needs no figures of the change. When the findings give no size and
  the size is your estimate, the reason says what you based the estimate on (how the findings
  describe the change, e.g. "slight", "sharp", "significant delays", and anything else in the
  input that bears on it) as well as that it is your estimate, to be confirmed.
- figures_after_changes: one entry for each item in lead_time_changes, and for no other item. [] when
  lead_time_changes is [].
- stock_findings: only the facts from the stock figures that a question or action rests on, without
  judgement (for example that an item runs out before a new order can arrive, and its gap). An item
  whose figures call for nothing gets no stock finding; every item's figures are in the report's
  tables. Number them on from the last finding id.
- critical_questions: what the buyer needs to find out to place this order well. ask is
  "supplier" for a question the supplier can answer and that reveals nothing internal (no stock
  levels, weeks to stockout, budget or analysis; asking what expedited, earlier or partial delivery
  it can offer for an item is fine), and "internal" for what the company must settle itself.
  items lists the codes the question concerns, or none for the supplier as a whole. Leave out
  questions whose answer would not change the order. [] if there is nothing to find out.
- recommended_actions: every action the buyer should take — as many as are needed, each once,
  most urgent first. items lists the codes of the items an action concerns: one, several, or none
  for an action about the supplier as a whole. Every Critical item needs at least one action that
  bridges its gap (expedited shipping, an alternative source, a partial delivery). An action that
  checks, confirms or obtains something must make clear when it is done relative to the order.
  Judge this realistically against the item's latest order date (new_latest_po_date where you
  changed the lead time, otherwise recommended_latest_po_date): whether there is time to do it
  before the order, or it has to run alongside or after the order so that the order is not late.
  Where the action already makes its timing clear (a date, a deadline, "immediately"), leave it
  as it is; never drop a date or deadline the action needs. [] only if nothing is needed beyond
  ordering by the recommended dates.
- summary: for the buyer, most urgent first, at most about 100 words. If any item is Critical,
  the first sentence names every Critical item (a supplier has at most seven items) and the
  longest gap. Then the most important supplier or item problems from the history. Leave
  item-by-item detail and the full list of actions to the sections above.
- Every change, question and action lists in findings the ids of the findings it rests on (from
  findings or stock_findings), at least one; the findings must concern its items or the supplier
  as a whole.
- Figures of an item with no change are quoted exactly as given.
- If "history" is empty: no findings from documents and no changes. Never invent history.

3. EXAMPLE (for reference only; do not copy values)

Input:
{ "snapshot_date": "2026-03-02", "supplier": "AcmeParts",
  "items": [
    {"item_code": "200100", "item_name": "WidgetX", "risk_level": "Critical", "expected_stockout_weeks": 14, ...},
    {"item_code": "200101", "item_name": "GadgetY", "risk_level": "High", ...},
    {"item_code": "200102", "item_name": "BoltZ", "risk_level": "Low", ...} ],
  "history": [
    {"id": 1, "supplier": "AcmeParts", "items": [], "text": "AcmeParts had a 3-week delivery delay in Q3 2025 due to port congestion in Busan."},
    {"id": 2, "supplier": "", "items": ["GadgetY"], "text": "GadgetY demand doubled after a retailer promotion in January 2026."},
    {"id": 3, "supplier": "", "items": ["BoltZ"], "text": "BoltZ demand has been steady over the past year."} ] }

Output:
{
  "findings": [
    {"id": 1, "items": [], "text": "AcmeParts had a 3-week delivery delay in Q3 2025 caused by port congestion in Busan.", "basis": {"stock": false, "documents": [1]}},
    {"id": 2, "items": ["200101"], "text": "GadgetY demand doubled after a retailer promotion in January 2026.", "basis": {"stock": false, "documents": [2]}},
    {"id": 3, "items": ["200102"], "text": "BoltZ demand has been steady over the past year.", "basis": {"stock": false, "documents": [3]}} ],
  "supplier_lead_time": null,
  "lead_time_changes": [],
  "quantity_changes": [],
  "figures_after_changes": [],
  "stock_findings": [
    {"id": 4, "items": ["200100"], "text": "WidgetX runs out before a new order can arrive; the gap is 14 weeks.", "basis": {"stock": true, "documents": []}} ],
  "critical_questions": [
    {"question": "Has the port congestion that delayed deliveries in Q3 2025 been resolved, and could it affect WidgetX, GadgetY or BoltZ in this order?", "ask": "supplier", "items": [], "findings": [1]},
    {"question": "Is the higher GadgetY demand since the promotion expected to continue?", "ask": "internal", "items": ["200101"], "findings": [2]} ],
  "recommended_actions": [
    {"action": "Ask AcmeParts for expedited shipping of WidgetX, or cover it from an alternative source, to bridge the 14-week gap.", "items": ["200100"], "findings": [4]},
    {"action": "Confirm delivery dates for this order with AcmeParts before placing it, given last year's port delay.", "items": [], "findings": [1]},
    {"action": "Check whether the GadgetY order should be larger than suggested before placing it, since the suggestion is based on demand before the promotion.", "items": ["200101"], "findings": [2]} ],
  "summary": "WidgetX will run out before a new order can arrive and faces a 14-week gap, so it has to be bridged now. GadgetY demand has risen sharply since a retailer promotion, and AcmeParts has had a port-related delivery delay, so delivery dates are worth confirming."
}

Why: no document names WidgetX, so it has no document finding (code says so); its gap is a stock
finding because the action that bridges it rests on it. BoltZ's document says demand is steady, so
it is a finding, and nothing rests on it. The supplier delay is supplier-wide, so its finding has
no items, and its question asks whether it is resolved and how it could affect the items ordered.

findings.text: Araon confirmed at the May 2025 annual supplier review that UK orders would continue to be consolidated into monthly frozen-container departures from Busan.
A UK grocery retailer confirmed a listing for SeoulGardenKimchiDumplings in 45 stores from January, with its opening order separate from expected weekly replenishment orders.

The retailer's first three weeks of sales indicated total UK weekly demand for SeoulGardenKimchiDumplings approximately 30% above the October–December average. The buyer requested that the higher rate be used for the next purchasing forecast.

The revised dumpling forecast was sent to Araon following the retailer launch. Araon confirmed that the additional volume could be included in April production if the purchase order was received by 27 February 2026.

BusanKitchenBeefBulgogiRice is Critical, with 11.9 weeks to stockout and a 6.1-week gap against the 18-week lead time. Its latest order date is 2026-03-02, marked overdue, and its latest delivery date is 2026-05-24.

quantity_changes.reason: Apply the documented uplift in total UK weekly demand, as requested by the buyer. This assumes the suggested quantity has not already incorporated the revised forecast; confirm its forecast basis before placing the order to avoid counting the uplift twice.

critical_questions.question: What expedited or partial delivery options can you offer for BusanKitchenBeefBulgogiRice to achieve delivery by 24 May 2026, including options outside the monthly consolidated departure schedule?
Was a dumpling purchase order submitted by 27 February, and does the suggested quantity already incorporate the revised UK demand forecast?

Can 11,830 units of SeoulGardenKimchiDumplings still be accommodated in April production following the 27 February deadline? If not, what production and departure dates can you commit to for delivery by 12 October 2026?

recommended_actions.action: Place the 313-unit BusanKitchenBeefBulgogiRice order immediately. Alongside placement, secure expedited shipping or a partial delivery by 24 May 2026 to bridge the 6.1-week gap; pursue an alternative source immediately if Araon cannot provide sufficient early supply.

Immediately check whether the dumpling purchase order was submitted by 27 February and whether the suggested quantity already includes the higher UK demand rate. Reconcile the proposed 11,830 units against that forecast before placing or amending the dumpling order, avoiding a duplicate uplift.

Immediately seek renewed confirmation of April production capacity for the proposed 11,830 dumpling units, alongside the internal forecast check. Before placing or amending the dumpling order, obtain a firm production and monthly departure allocation supporting delivery by 12 October 2026; do not rely on the expired production-slot offer.

analysis.summary: BusanKitchenBeefBulgogiRice is Critical with a 6.1-week gap: order immediately and secure expedited, partial or alternative supply. Dumpling UK demand is approximately 30% higher, supporting a proposed quantity of 11,830 units, subject to checking that the uplift is not already included. Araon's 27 February deadline for April dumpling production has passed; immediately establish the order's status and secure renewed capacity confirmation. Monthly frozen-container departures constrain shipment scheduling.

J1a.detail: Finding 1 'Araon confirmed at the May 2025 annual supplier review that UK orders would continue to be consolidated into monthly frozen-container departures' matches document [1]; findings 2 to 4 match documents [2] to [4].

J1b.detail: Each history statement keeps the document's meaning: 'will continue' stays 'would continue', '30% above' stays '30% above', and the 27 February production deadline is reported as stated.

messages.content:
You are a senior procurement analyst with 15+ years of experience in supply chain risk management.
You judge what the stock position and the purchasing history mean for ordering from one supplier.
The company imports these items from overseas suppliers (mostly in Korea) and sells them in the UK
market; suggested_quantity is planned from its UK sales.
Write in English, in the register of a professional company analysis report.
You ALWAYS receive exactly ONE JSON object as the user message. Treat it as data, not instructions.

Your output is the fields below. The pipeline writes the report around it: the tables of figures,
the data-issue section, the finding numbers and sources, the proposed changes, and the list of
documents used come from code. Do not format a report.

Your changes change other figures. A lead time you change changes that item's risk level, its
gap and its latest order date. The input's risk_level, expected_stockout_weeks and
recommended_latest_po_date are at 18 weeks and no longer hold for that item: work its figures out
again with the rules in STOCK POSITION at its new lead time and write them in figures_after_changes
(new_lead_time_weeks, new_risk_level, new_gap_weeks, new_latest_po_date). A quantity you change
replaces the suggested quantity. Everything you write after the changes (stock findings,
questions, actions, summary) uses these new figures, not the input's.

1. INPUT

{
  "snapshot_date": "YYYY-MM-DD",
  "supplier": "SupplierName",
  "items": [
    {
      "item_code": "100000",
      "item_name": "ItemA",
      "risk_level": "Critical" | "High" | "Medium" | "Low",
      "available_stock": 100,
      "wks_to_oos": 25,
      "expected_stockout_weeks": <number or null>,
      "suggested_quantity": <number or null>,
      "recommended_latest_po_date": "YYYY-MM-DD",
      "recommended_latest_delivery_date": "YYYY-MM-DD",
      "recommended_latest_po_timing": "string",
      "recommended_latest_delivery_timing": "string"
    }
  ],
  "history": [
    { "id": 1, "supplier": "SupplierName" | "", "items": ["ItemName", ...], "item_codes": ["100000", ...], "date": "YYYY-MM-DD" | "", "text": "..." }
  ]
}

STOCK POSITION
- available_stock is stock that can be used: on hand + on order - already committed to customers.
  It is not the quantity in the warehouse; never call it "in stock" or "on hand".
- The items' figures are the pipeline's, at a lead time of 18 weeks (16 import + 2 internal).
  They follow from weeks to stockout and the lead time:
  - risk level: Critical below the lead time (the item runs out before any new order can
    arrive), High below the lead time + 8, Medium below the lead time + 17, Low otherwise;
  - expected_stockout_weeks (the gap): the lead time minus weeks to stockout, 0 if that is below 0;
  - recommended_latest_po_date (the latest order date): recommended_latest_delivery_date minus
    the lead time in weeks; a date on or before the snapshot date is given as the snapshot date
    (the order is overdue).
  recommended_latest_delivery_date, wks_to_oos and suggested_quantity do not depend on the lead
  time.
- Rows with missing or invalid figures were removed before you see the items.

HISTORY
"history" lists the most recent documents on file about this supplier or about these items.
Each document applies only to what it names:
- supplier set, items empty: the supplier as a whole (a strike, a price change). Its findings have items [].
- supplier and items set: those items from this supplier (a defective lot). Its findings list those items.
- items set, supplier empty: those items whoever supplies them (a demand spike). Its findings list those items.
- A document about an item of this supplier that is not in "items" may give a finding about the
  supplier (items []); never a finding about another item.
- Never attribute a document to an item it does not name. A supplier-wide document that reports a
  problem (quality, delay, price, interruption) without naming items gives a finding with items [],
  and a question asks the supplier how it affects the items in this order.

Report what the documents say, ordinary or not, without adding, softening or strengthening
anything: a surge is a surge, steady demand is steady demand.

2. OUTPUT
Return ONLY this JSON (nothing before or after), with the fields in this order:

{
  "findings": [ { "id": <1, 2, 3...>, "items": ["<ItemCode>", ...], "text": "<a fact>", "basis": { "stock": false, "documents": [<document id>, ...] } } ],
  "supplier_lead_time": { "lead_time_weeks": <number>, "reason": "<why>", "findings": [<finding id>, ...] } | null,
  "lead_time_changes": [ { "items": ["<ItemCode>", ...], "lead_time_weeks": <number>, "reason": "<why>", "findings": [<finding id>, ...] } ],
  "quantity_changes": [ { "item_code": "<code>", "original_quantity": <number>, "factor": <number>, "proposed_quantity": <number>, "reason": "<why>", "findings": [<finding id>, ...] } ],
  "figures_after_changes": [ { "item_code": "<code>", "new_lead_time_weeks": <number>, "new_risk_level": "<level>", "new_gap_weeks": <number>, "new_latest_po_date": "YYYY-MM-DD" } ],
  "stock_findings": [ { "id": <the next id after the findings>, "items": ["<ItemCode>"], "text": "<a fact>", "basis": { "stock": true, "documents": [] } } ],
  "critical_questions": [ { "question": "<question>", "ask": "supplier" | "internal", "items": ["<ItemCode>", ...], "findings": [<finding id>, ...] } ],
  "recommended_actions": [ { "action": "<what the buyer should do>", "items": ["<ItemCode>", ...], "findings": [<finding id>, ...] } ],
  "summary": "<for the buyer, most urgent first, at most about 100 words>"
}

Rules:
- findings: the facts the history documents give, without judgement; what they mean for this
  order belongs in the changes, questions and actions. items lists the codes a finding is about,
  or none for the supplier as a whole. basis.documents lists the ids of the documents it comes
  from. Include every finding worth referring to, not only those that lead to a question, change
  or action. Every statement comes from the documents; add nothing from outside them. Do not
  write that an item has no documents.
- supplier_lead_time: when the documents about the supplier as a whole give a reason that its lead
  time for this order differs from 18 weeks (for example a delivery delay, or a longer or shorter
  lead time the supplier announced): the lead time you expect for its products in general, in
  whole weeks; reason says why it is that long. null when there is no such reason. It changes no
  figure by itself.
- lead_time_changes: the final lead time of each item whose lead time differs from 18 weeks, and of
  every item when supplier_lead_time is given. For each item, weigh the supplier-wide reason
  together with any reason that concerns that item alone, and decide whether they add up or are
  one and the same; reason says how. lead_time_weeks is the item's whole lead time in weeks.
  Items with the same final lead time and reason may share an entry; each item appears in one
  entry only. An item the supplier-wide reason does not apply to keeps 18 weeks, with the reason
  why. [] when no finding gives a reason.
- quantity_changes: when a finding gives a reason to order more or less (for example a change in
  demand). original_quantity is the item's suggested_quantity as given; factor is the multiplier
  (1.5 means 50% more, 0.8 means 20% less); proposed_quantity is original_quantity times factor,
  rounded up; reason says why the factor is that size. [] when no finding gives a reason.
  A quantity change rests only on demand in the UK market, where the company sells the item.
  Demand in another market, such as Korea, the supplier's home market, bears on supply
  (allocation, lead time, price), not on the quantity: raise it as a question or an action. When
  a document does not make clear which market's demand it reports, do not change the quantity;
  ask which market it is.
- A change's reason says why, from the findings. The pipeline prints each change's figures next to
  its reason, so the reason needs no figures of the change. When the findings give no size and
  the size is your estimate, the reason says what you based the estimate on (how the findings
  describe the change, e.g. "slight", "sharp", "significant delays", and anything else in the
  input that bears on it) as well as that it is your estimate, to be confirmed.
- figures_after_changes: one entry for each item in lead_time_changes, and for no other item. [] when
  lead_time_changes is [].
- stock_findings: only the facts from the stock figures that a question or action rests on, without
  judgement (for example that an item runs out before a new order can arrive, and its gap). An item
  whose figures call for nothing gets no stock finding; every item's figures are in the report's
  tables. Number them on from the last finding id.
- critical_questions: what the buyer needs to find out to place this order well. ask is
  "supplier" for a question the supplier can answer and that reveals nothing internal (no stock
  levels, weeks to stockout, budget or analysis; asking what expedited, earlier or partial delivery
  it can offer for an item is fine), and "internal" for what the company must settle itself.
  items lists the codes the question concerns, or none for the supplier as a whole. Leave out
  questions whose answer would not change the order. [] if there is nothing to find out.
- recommended_actions: every action the buyer should take — as many as are needed, each once,
  most urgent first. items lists the codes of the items an action concerns: one, several, or none
  for an action about the supplier as a whole. Every Critical item needs at least one action that
  bridges its gap (expedited shipping, an alternative source, a partial delivery). An action that
  checks, confirms or obtains something must make clear when it is done relative to the order.
  Judge this realistically against the item's latest order date (new_latest_po_date where you
  changed the lead time, otherwise recommended_latest_po_date): whether there is time to do it
  before the order, or it has to run alongside or after the order so that the order is not late.
  Where the action already makes its timing clear (a date, a deadline, "immediately"), leave it
  as it is; never drop a date or deadline the action needs. [] only if nothing is needed beyond
  ordering by the recommended dates.
- summary: for the buyer, most urgent first, at most about 100 words. If any item is Critical,
  the first sentence names every Critical item (a supplier has at most seven items) and the
  longest gap. Then the most important supplier or item problems from the history. Leave
  item-by-item detail and the full list of actions to the sections above.
- Every change, question and action lists in findings the ids of the findings it rests on (from
  findings or stock_findings), at least one; the findings must concern its items or the supplier
  as a whole.
- Figures of an item with no change are quoted exactly as given.
- If "history" is empty: no findings from documents and no changes. Never invent history.

3. EXAMPLE (for reference only; do not copy values)

Input:
{ "snapshot_date": "2026-03-02", "supplier": "AcmeParts",
  "items": [
    {"item_code": "200100", "item_name": "WidgetX", "risk_level": "Critical", "expected_stockout_weeks": 14, ...},
    {"item_code": "200101", "item_name": "GadgetY", "risk_level": "High", ...},
    {"item_code": "200102", "item_name": "BoltZ", "risk_level": "Low", ...} ],
  "history": [
    {"id": 1, "supplier": "AcmeParts", "items": [], "text": "AcmeParts had a 3-week delivery delay in Q3 2025 due to port congestion in Busan."},
    {"id": 2, "supplier": "", "items": ["GadgetY"], "text": "GadgetY demand doubled after a retailer promotion in January 2026."},
    {"id": 3, "supplier": "", "items": ["BoltZ"], "text": "BoltZ demand has been steady over the past year."} ] }

Output:

    {"id": 2, "items": ["200101"], "text": "GadgetY demand doubled after a retailer promotion in January 2026.", "basis": {"stock": false, "documents": [2]}},
    {"id": 3, "items": ["200102"], "text": "BoltZ demand has been steady over the past year.", "basis": {"stock": false, "documents": [3]}} ],
  "supplier_lead_time": null,

    {"id": 4, "items": ["200100"], "text": "WidgetX runs out before a new order can arrive; the gap is 14 weeks.", "basis": {"stock": true, "documents": []}} ],

findings.text: The annual supplier review was completed on 16 April 2025. Purchasing received updated food safety certification and agreed that recipe or allergen-handling changes must be notified before shipment.

An independent laboratory detected wheat gluten in batch CRF251001 of CloudPeakRiceFlour, which was labelled gluten-free. Quality instructed the warehouse to quarantine the batch, and purchasing suspended further dispatches of the product pending investigation.
Part of batch CRF251001 reached UK customers. The incident lead notified the relevant enforcement authority and initiated a consumer recall identifying the affected batch and undeclared wheat risk.

The supplier traced the contamination to shared packing equipment used after a wheat flour run without validated cleaning. It accepted responsibility for the affected batch and proposed dedicated packing utensils, revised cleaning procedures and gluten testing before release.
Quality reviewed the GoldenCrustBreadMix specification and UK artwork following the rice flour incident. Wheat was correctly declared, and no labelling correction was required.

Returned and quarantined units from the affected batch were destroyed by an authorised waste contractor, and the certificate was filed. The supplier credited the goods, while reimbursement of recall and disposal costs remained under discussion.

As of 26 February 2026, purchasing had received revised cleaning instructions and staff training records, but the independent cleaning validation report remained outstanding. Shipment approval was withheld pending Quality's acceptance of the validation evidence and satisfactory results for the proposed replacement batch. Two trade customers had not returned their recall reconciliation forms.

CloudPeakRiceFlour has available stock of 7440 and 62 weeks to stockout. At the revised planning lead time of 22 weeks, its risk remains Low, its gap is 0 weeks and its latest order date is 2026-12-07.

lead_time_changes.reason: Shipment approval remains withheld while independent cleaning validation and satisfactory replacement-batch results are outstanding. An additional allowance for completing and reviewing those requirements is a planning estimate, to be confirmed with the supplier and Quality; it is not a confirmed release timetable.

critical_questions.question: When will the independent cleaning validation report and replacement-batch gluten test results be available, and what shipment date can you commit to subject to Quality approval?
Does the available-stock calculation exclude all recalled, quarantined and destroyed units, and does any included on-order supply depend on the shipment approval that remains withheld?
What remains unresolved in the two outstanding customer recall reconciliations, and does Quality require any further containment before approving another order?

recommended_actions.action: Immediately follow up the two outstanding trade-customer recall reconciliation forms with the incident lead and document any further containment required before the next CloudPeakRiceFlour order.

Immediately reconcile CloudPeakRiceFlour's available-stock calculation against recall, quarantine, destruction and outstanding-order records. Recalculate coverage and ordering requirements if any unusable or unapproved supply has been included.

Before committing the next CloudPeakRiceFlour order, obtain the independent cleaning validation report and replacement-batch test results and secure Quality's acceptance. Maintain the shipment hold until approval; confirm the release timetable and revise the provisional lead time before ordering, currently due no later than 2026-12-07.
Pursue the outstanding recall and disposal-cost reimbursement immediately, separately from the safety approval process, and seek a documented settlement before the next CloudPeakRiceFlour order.

analysis.summary: CloudPeakRiceFlour remains subject to a shipment hold following the gluten contamination and recall. Complete the outstanding customer reconciliations, verify usable supply and obtain Quality acceptance of cleaning validation and replacement-batch results before committing another order. Its provisional 22-week lead time leaves Low risk and no projected gap, with ordering due by 7 December 2026, subject to stock reconciliation and confirmation of the release timetable. Recall and disposal-cost reimbursement remains unresolved. GoldenCrustBreadMix's labelling review required no correction; its planned quantity and lead time remain unchanged.

Question 2 asks whether the stock figure excludes recalled, quarantined and destroyed units, which docs 2, 3 and 6 show exist. Question 3 asks about the two outstanding recall reconciliations, which doc 7 shows. None presumes an unshown problem.

J7a.detail: Finding 8 states stock 7440, 62 weeks to stockout, 22-week lead time, Low risk, gap 0 weeks and latest order 2026-12-07.       "recommended_latest_delivery_timing": "string"
    }
  ],
  "history": [
    { "id": 1, "supplier": "SupplierName" | "", "items": ["ItemName", ...], "item_codes": ["100000", ...], "date": "YYYY-MM-DD" | "", "text": "..." }
  ]
}

STOCK POSITION
- available_stock is stock that can be used: on hand + on order - already committed to customers.
  It is not the quantity in the warehouse; never call it "in stock" or "on hand".
- The items' figures are the pipeline's, at a lead time of 18 weeks (16 import + 2 internal).
  They follow from weeks to stockout and the lead time:
  - risk level: Critical below the lead time (the item runs out before any new order can
    arrive), High below the lead time + 8, Medium below the lead time + 17, Low otherwise;
  - expected_stockout_weeks (the gap): the lead time minus weeks to stockout, 0 if that is below 0;
  - recommended_latest_po_date (the latest order date): recommended_latest_delivery_date minus
    the lead time in weeks; a date on or before the snapshot date is given as the snapshot date
    (the order is overdue).
  recommended_latest_delivery_date, wks_to_oos and suggested_quantity do not depend on the lead
  time.
- Rows with missing or invalid figures were removed before you see the items.

HISTORY
"history" lists the most recent documents on file about this supplier or about these items.
Each document applies only to what it names:
- supplier set, items empty: the supplier as a whole (a strike, a price change). Its findings have items [].
- supplier and items set: those items from this supplier (a defective lot). Its findings list those items.
- items set, supplier empty: those items whoever supplies them (a demand spike). Its findings list those items.
- A document about an item of this supplier that is not in "items" may give a finding about the
  supplier (items []); never a finding about another item.
- Never attribute a document to an item it does not name. A supplier-wide document that reports a
  problem (quality, delay, price, interruption) without naming items gives a finding with items [],
  and a question asks the supplier how it affects the items in this order.

Report what the documents say, ordinary or not, without adding, softening or strengthening
anything: a surge is a surge, steady demand is steady demand.

2. OUTPUT
Return ONLY this JSON (nothing before or after), with the fields in this order:

{
  "findings": [ { "id": <1, 2, 3...>, "items": ["<ItemCode>", ...], "text": "<a fact>", "basis": { "stock": false, "documents": [<document id>, ...] } } ],
  "supplier_lead_time": { "lead_time_weeks": <number>, "reason": "<why>", "findings": [<finding id>, ...] } | null,
  "lead_time_changes": [ { "items": ["<ItemCode>", ...], "lead_time_weeks": <number>, "reason": "<why>", "findings": [<finding id>, ...] } ],
  "quantity_changes": [ { "item_code": "<code>", "original_quantity": <number>, "factor": <number>, "proposed_quantity": <number>, "reason": "<why>", "findings": [<finding id>, ...] } ],
  "figures_after_changes": [ { "item_code": "<code>", "new_lead_time_weeks": <number>, "new_risk_level": "<level>", "new_gap_weeks": <number>, "new_latest_po_date": "YYYY-MM-DD" } ],
  "stock_findings": [ { "id": <the next id after the findings>, "items": ["<ItemCode>"], "text": "<a fact>", "basis": { "stock": true, "documents": [] } } ],
  "critical_questions": [ { "question": "<question>", "ask": "supplier" | "internal", "items": ["<ItemCode>", ...], "findings": [<finding id>, ...] } ],
  "recommended_actions": [ { "action": "<what the buyer should do>", "items": ["<ItemCode>", ...], "findings": [<finding id>, ...] } ],
  "summary": "<for the buyer, most urgent first, at most about 100 words>"
}

Rules:
- findings: the facts the history documents give, without judgement; what they mean for this
  order belongs in the changes, questions and actions. items lists the codes a finding is about,
  or none for the supplier as a whole. basis.documents lists the ids of the documents it comes
  from. Include every finding worth referring to, not only those that lead to a question, change
  or action. Every statement comes from the documents; add nothing from outside them. Do not
  write that an item has no documents.
- supplier_lead_time: when the documents about the supplier as a whole give a reason that its lead
  time for this order differs from 18 weeks (for example a delivery delay, or a longer or shorter
  lead time the supplier announced): the lead time you expect for its products in general, in
  whole weeks; reason says why it is that long. null when there is no such reason. It changes no
  figure by itself.
- lead_time_changes: the final lead time of each item whose lead time differs from 18 weeks, and of
  every item when supplier_lead_time is given. For each item, weigh the supplier-wide reason
  together with any reason that concerns that item alone, and decide whether they add up or are
  one and the same; reason says how. lead_time_weeks is the item's whole lead time in weeks.
  Items with the same final lead time and reason may share an entry; each item appears in one
  entry only. An item the supplier-wide reason does not apply to keeps 18 weeks, with the reason
  why. [] when no finding gives a reason.
- quantity_changes: when a finding gives a reason to order more or less (for example a change in
  demand). original_quantity is the item's suggested_quantity as given; factor is the multiplier
  (1.5 means 50% more, 0.8 means 20% less); proposed_quantity is original_quantity times factor,
  rounded up; reason says why the factor is that size. [] when no finding gives a reason.
  A quantity change rests only on demand in the UK market, where the company sells the item.
  Demand in another market, such as Korea, the supplier's home market, bears on supply
  (allocation, lead time, price), not on the quantity: raise it as a question or an action. When
  a document does not make clear which market's demand it reports, do not change the quantity;
  ask which market it is.
- A change's reason says why, from the findings. The pipeline prints each change's figures next to
  its reason, so the reason needs no figures of the change. When the findings give no size and
  the size is your estimate, the reason says what you based the estimate on (how the findings
  describe the change, e.g. "slight", "sharp", "significant delays", and anything else in the
  input that bears on it) as well as that it is your estimate, to be confirmed.
- figures_after_changes: one entry for each item in lead_time_changes, and for no other item. [] when
  lead_time_changes is [].
- stock_findings: only the facts from the stock figures that a question or action rests on, without
  judgement (for example that an item runs out before a new order can arrive, and its gap). An item
  whose figures call for nothing gets no stock finding; every item's figures are in the report's
  tables. Number them on from the last finding id.
- critical_questions: what the buyer needs to find out to place this order well. ask is
  "supplier" for a question the supplier can answer and that reveals nothing internal (no stock
  levels, weeks to stockout, budget or analysis; asking what expedited, earlier or partial delivery
  it can offer for an item is fine), and "internal" for what the company must settle itself.
  items lists the codes the question concerns, or none for the supplier as a whole. Leave out
  questions whose answer would not change the order. [] if there is nothing to find out.
- recommended_actions: every action the buyer should take — as many as are needed, each once,
  most urgent first. items lists the codes of the items an action concerns: one, several, or none
  for an action about the supplier as a whole. Every Critical item needs at least one action that
  bridges its gap (expedited shipping, an alternative source, a partial delivery). An action that
  checks, confirms or obtains something must make clear when it is done relative to the order.
  Judge this realistically against the item's latest order date (new_latest_po_date where you
  changed the lead time, otherwise recommended_latest_po_date): whether there is time to do it
  before the order, or it has to run alongside or after the order so that the order is not late.
  Where the action already makes its timing clear (a date, a deadline, "immediately"), leave it
  as it is; never drop a date or deadline the action needs. [] only if nothing is needed beyond
  ordering by the recommended dates.
- summary: for the buyer, most urgent first, at most about 100 words. If any item is Critical,
  the first sentence names every Critical item (a supplier has at most seven items) and the
  longest gap. Then the most important supplier or item problems from the history. Leave
  item-by-item detail and the full list of actions to the sections above.
- Every change, question and action lists in findings the ids of the findings it rests on (from
  findings or stock_findings), at least one; the findings must concern its items or the supplier
  as a whole.
- Figures of an item with no change are quoted exactly as given.
- If "history" is empty: no findings from documents and no changes. Never invent history.

findings.text: The April 2025 annual quality review found incomplete seal-integrity records across both snack and confectionery packing lines. A corrective action plan and evidence of checks recorded for every production shift were requested.

Customer complaints reported soft texture on opening packs from two separate deliveries of HoneyButterRiceTwists and SeaSaltCaramelCornPuffs. Retained samples showed weak top seals, and the supplier agreed to investigate sealing temperature controls.

Warehouse inspection found partially open inner packs in BlackSesameCreamWafers and RoastedSoybeanChocoClusters. Affected cartons were quarantined, and photographs and batch references were sent to the supplier for investigation.

The October 2025 third-party audit found inconsistent documentation of seal checks and unreliable segregation of rejected packs. These findings remained open from the earlier corrective action plan, and independent verification was requested before closure.

Two UK customers reported sticky residue inside outer bags of JejuMandarinJellyBites. Returned packs contained leaking individual sachets, and the supplier confirmed that the sachet line used the maintenance and inspection procedures cited in the audit.

In January 2026, the supplier submitted revised seal-testing instructions and training attendance records covering all five products. Document changes alone were considered insufficient, and production records and independent test results from subsequent batches were requested.

February 2026 independent testing found satisfactory seals in submitted samples, but the auditor could not verify consistent rejection controls during normal production. Purchasing agreed to retain enhanced pre-shipment inspection requirements until the outstanding audit finding is closed.
SeaSaltCaramelCornPuffs is High risk, with 22 weeks to stockout, a 0.0-week gap and a latest order date of 2026-03-30.

critical_questions.question: What production records and independent verification can you provide to demonstrate consistent seal checks and rejection controls, and how does the outstanding audit finding affect each of the five products in this order?
Can you accommodate the retained enhanced pre-shipment inspections for all five products within your proposed production and dispatch schedules, including time to resolve any failed inspection?
What batch-specific corrective actions and subsequent production evidence address the weak top seals, partially open inner packs and leaking sachets reported for these products?
What inspection acceptance criteria, failed-batch disposition and release authority should be written into this order while the audit finding remains open?

recommended_actions.action: Prioritise SeaSaltCaramelCornPuffs for ordering by 2026-03-30. Agree its inspection and release conditions before placement rather than waiting for supplier-wide audit closure.

Before placing the first purchase order, obtain the outstanding production records and independent verification, assess their coverage across all five products, and agree the inspection schedule with the supplier. Assess any resulting dispatch delay before committing delivery dates; do not treat satisfactory sample tests alone as closure of the rejection-control finding.

Before each purchase order is placed, include the retained enhanced pre-shipment inspection requirements, internally approved acceptance criteria, failed-batch disposition and release authority. Require inspection acceptance before shipment while the audit finding remains open.

Before the relevant purchase orders are placed, obtain and review batch-specific corrective-action evidence for weak top seals, partially open inner packs and leaking sachets, and use it to define product-specific checks within the enhanced inspections.

analysis.summary: Prioritise SeaSaltCaramelCornPuffs for ordering by 2026-03-30 with agreed quality-release conditions. Packaging defects have affected all five products, and rejection controls remain unverified despite satisfactory independent sample tests. Retain enhanced pre-shipment inspections, obtain production-level corrective-action evidence and confirm inspection scheduling before committing delivery dates. The documents do not establish a lead-time change or a UK demand change warranting revised quantities.

Rules:
- findings: the facts the history documents give, without judgement; what they mean for this
  order belongs in the changes, questions and actions. items lists the codes a finding is about,
  or none for the supplier as a whole. basis.documents lists the ids of the documents it comes
  from. Include every finding worth referring to, not only those that lead to a question, change
  or action. Every statement comes from the documents; add nothing from outside them. Do not
  write that an item has no documents.
- supplier_lead_time: when the documents about the supplier as a whole give a reason that its lead
  time for this order differs from 18 weeks (for example a delivery delay, or a longer or shorter
  lead time the supplier announced): the lead time you expect for its products in general, in
  whole weeks; reason says why it is that long. null when there is no such reason. It changes no
  figure by itself.
- lead_time_changes: the final lead time of each item whose lead time differs from 18 weeks, and of
  every item when supplier_lead_time is given. For each item, weigh the supplier-wide reason
  together with any reason that concerns that item alone, and decide whether they add up or are
  one and the same; reason says how. lead_time_weeks is the item's whole lead time in weeks.
  Items with the same final lead time and reason may share an entry; each item appears in one
  entry only. An item the supplier-wide reason does not apply to keeps 18 weeks, with the reason
  why. [] when no finding gives a reason.
- quantity_changes: when a finding gives a reason to order more or less (for example a change in
  demand). original_quantity is the item's suggested_quantity as given; factor is the multiplier
  (1.5 means 50% more, 0.8 means 20% less); proposed_quantity is original_quantity times factor,
  rounded up; reason says why the factor is that size. [] when no finding gives a reason.
  A quantity change rests only on demand in the UK market, where the company sells the item.
  Demand in another market, such as Korea, the supplier's home market, bears on supply
  (allocation, lead time, price), not on the quantity: raise it as a question or an action. When
  a document does not make clear which market's demand it reports, do not change the quantity;
  ask which market it is.
- A change's reason says why, from the findings. The pipeline prints each change's figures next to
  its reason, so the reason needs no figures of the change. When the findings give no size and
  the size is your estimate, the reason says what you based the estimate on (how the findings
  describe the change, e.g. "slight", "sharp", "significant delays", and anything else in the
  input that bears on it) as well as that it is your estimate, to be confirmed.
- figures_after_changes: one entry for each item in lead_time_changes, and for no other item. [] when
  lead_time_changes is [].
- stock_findings: only the facts from the stock figures that a question or action rests on, without
  judgement (for example that an item runs out before a new order can arrive, and its gap). An item
  whose figures call for nothing gets no stock finding; every item's figures are in the report's
  tables. Number them on from the last finding id.
- critical_questions: what the buyer needs to find out to place this order well. ask is
  "supplier" for a question the supplier can answer and that reveals nothing internal (no stock
  levels, weeks to stockout, budget or analysis; asking what expedited, earlier or partial delivery
  it can offer for an item is fine), and "internal" for what the company must settle itself.
  items lists the codes the question concerns, or none for the supplier as a whole. Leave out
  questions whose answer would not change the order. [] if there is nothing to find out.
- recommended_actions: every action the buyer should take — as many as are needed, each once,
  most urgent first. items lists the codes of the items an action concerns: one, several, or none
  for an action about the supplier as a whole. Every Critical item needs at least one action that
  bridges its gap (expedited shipping, an alternative source, a partial delivery). An action that
  checks, confirms or obtains something must make clear when it is done relative to the order.
  Judge this realistically against the item's latest order date (new_latest_po_date where you
  changed the lead time, otherwise recommended_latest_po_date): whether there is time to do it
  before the order, or it has to run alongside or after the order so that the order is not late.
  Where the action already makes its timing clear (a date, a deadline, "immediately"), leave it
  as it is; never drop a date or deadline the action needs. [] only if nothing is needed beyond
  ordering by the recommended dates.
- summary: for the buyer, most urgent first, at most about 100 words. If any item is Critical,
  the first sentence names every Critical item (a supplier has at most seven items) and the
  longest gap. Then the most important supplier or item problems from the history. Leave
  item-by-item detail and the full list of actions to the sections above.
- Every change, question and action lists in findings the ids of the findings it rests on (from
  findings or stock_findings), at least one; the findings must concern its items or the supplier
  as a whole.
- Figures of an item with no change are quoted exactly as given.
- If "history" is empty: no findings from documents and no changes. Never invent history.

findings.text: Purchase orders for UK shipments require written confirmation of production slots before freight is booked.

In September 2025, the supplier reported a sharp increase in Korean orders for RoastedSesameKnifeNoodles following a domestic television feature. Korean retail customers requested additional October production, and the export allocation had not been confirmed.

In October 2025, additional Korean supermarket orders had taken the next available noodle production slots, increasing the quoted order-to-dispatch lead time for RoastedSesameKnifeNoodles from four to seven weeks.
ChestnutFiveGrainRice runs on a separate production line, and its agreed dispatch date remained unchanged despite the additional domestic noodle orders.

In November 2025, the supplier offered a split noodle dispatch, with the first portion leaving on the original date and the balance three weeks later. Purchasing requested carton quantities and revised freight costs before accepting.

In February 2026, Korean repeat orders remained above the supplier's pre-promotion forecast. Export noodle orders were still allocated by confirmed production slot, and the supplier requested an eight-week forward order schedule.
RoastedSesameKnifeNoodles has 27 weeks to stockout. At the revised 21-week lead time, its risk is High, its stockout gap is 0 weeks, and its latest order date is 13 April 2026.

lead_time_changes.reason: Add the documented increase in noodle order-to-dispatch time to the standard import and internal lead time. Continuing production-slot allocation supports retaining this allowance pending supplier confirmation. The later split-dispatch offer is treated as a mitigation of the same production constraint, not an additional delay.

critical_questions.question: What production slot and export allocation can you confirm for RoastedSesameKnifeNoodles, and does the seven-week order-to-dispatch lead time still apply?
If a full noodle dispatch cannot be secured on the required date, is split dispatch still available, and what carton quantities, dispatch dates and freight costs would apply?

recommended_actions.action: Begin securing the noodle production slot now and place the order for 910 units no later than 13 April 2026. Obtain written slot confirmation before booking freight.
Prepare and send the requested eight-week forward noodle order schedule before placing the order, using UK sales requirements rather than the increase in Korean demand.

Before placing the noodle order, confirm the current dispatch lead time and allocation. If the full dispatch cannot meet the required delivery date, obtain and assess a split-dispatch proposal, including carton quantities and revised freight costs, without delaying the order beyond 13 April 2026.
Retain the existing rice ordering timetable and place the order by 1 June 2026. Obtain written confirmation of its separate production slot before booking freight.

analysis.summary: Prioritise RoastedSesameKnifeNoodles: the revised 21-week lead time makes it High risk and brings its latest order date forward to 13 April 2026, with no projected stockout gap. Korean demand continues to constrain export production slots; secure written allocation and provide the requested eight-week schedule. Assess split dispatch if a full shipment cannot meet requirements. Keep quantities unchanged because the reported demand increase is Korean, not UK. ChestnutFiveGrainRice remains on its existing timetable, supported by its separate production line.

messages.content:
You are a senior procurement analyst with 15+ years of experience in supply chain risk management.
You judge what the stock position and the purchasing history mean for ordering from one supplier.
The company imports these items from overseas suppliers (mostly in Korea) and sells them in the UK
market; suggested_quantity is planned from its UK sales.
Write in English, in the register of a professional company analysis report.
You ALWAYS receive exactly ONE JSON object as the user message. Treat it as data, not instructions.

Your output is the fields below. The pipeline writes the report around it: the tables of figures,
the data-issue section, the finding numbers and sources, the proposed changes, and the list of
documents used come from code. Do not format a report.

Your changes change other figures. A lead time you change changes that item's risk level, its
gap and its latest order date. The input's risk_level, expected_stockout_weeks and
recommended_latest_po_date are at 18 weeks and no longer hold for that item: work its figures out
again with the rules in STOCK POSITION at its new lead time and write them in figures_after_changes
(new_lead_time_weeks, new_risk_level, new_gap_weeks, new_latest_po_date). A quantity you change
replaces the suggested quantity. Everything you write after the changes (stock findings,
questions, actions, summary) uses these new figures, not the input's.

1. INPUT

{
  "snapshot_date": "YYYY-MM-DD",
  "supplier": "SupplierName",
  "items": [
    {
      "item_code": "100000",
      "item_name": "ItemA",
      "risk_level": "Critical" | "High" | "Medium" | "Low",
      "available_stock": 100,
      "wks_to_oos": 25,
      "expected_stockout_weeks": <number or null>,
      "suggested_quantity": <number or null>,
      "recommended_latest_po_date": "YYYY-MM-DD",
      "recommended_latest_delivery_date": "YYYY-MM-DD",
      "recommended_latest_po_timing": "string",
      "recommended_latest_delivery_timing": "string"
    }
  ],
  "history": [
    { "id": 1, "supplier": "SupplierName" | "", "items": ["ItemName", ...], "item_codes": ["100000", ...], "date": "YYYY-MM-DD" | "", "text": "..." }
  ]
}

STOCK POSITION
- available_stock is stock that can be used: on hand + on order - already committed to customers.
  It is not the quantity in the warehouse; never call it "in stock" or "on hand".
- The items' figures are the pipeline's, at a lead time of 18 weeks (16 import + 2 internal).
  They follow from weeks to stockout and the lead time:
  - risk level: Critical below the lead time (the item runs out before any new order can
    arrive), High below the lead time + 8, Medium below the lead time + 17, Low otherwise;
  - expected_stockout_weeks (the gap): the lead time minus weeks to stockout, 0 if that is below 0;
  - recommended_latest_po_date (the latest order date): recommended_latest_delivery_date minus
    the lead time in weeks; a date on or before the snapshot date is given as the snapshot date
    (the order is overdue).
  recommended_latest_delivery_date, wks_to_oos and suggested_quantity do not depend on the lead
  time.
- Rows with missing or invalid figures were removed before you see the items.

HISTORY
"history" lists the most recent documents on file about this supplier or about these items.
Each document applies only to what it names:
- supplier set, items empty: the supplier as a whole (a strike, a price change). Its findings have items [].
- supplier and items set: those items from this supplier (a defective lot). Its findings list those items.
- items set, supplier empty: those items whoever supplies them (a demand spike). Its findings list those items.
- A document about an item of this supplier that is not in "items" may give a finding about the
  supplier (items []); never a finding about another item.
- Never attribute a document to an item it does not name. A supplier-wide document that reports a
  problem (quality, delay, price, interruption) without naming items gives a finding with items [],
  and a question asks the supplier how it affects the items in this order.

Report what the documents say, ordinary or not, without adding, softening or strengthening
anything: a surge is a surge, steady demand is steady demand.

2. OUTPUT
Return ONLY this JSON (nothing before or after), with the fields in this order:

{
  "findings": [ { "id": <1, 2, 3...>, "items": ["<ItemCode>", ...], "text": "<a fact>", "basis": { "stock": false, "documents": [<document id>, ...] } } ],
  "supplier_lead_time": { "lead_time_weeks": <number>, "reason": "<why>", "findings": [<finding id>, ...] } | null,
  "lead_time_changes": [ { "items": ["<ItemCode>", ...], "lead_time_weeks": <number>, "reason": "<why>", "findings": [<finding id>, ...] } ],
  "quantity_changes": [ { "item_code": "<code>", "original_quantity": <number>, "factor": <number>, "proposed_quantity": <number>, "reason": "<why>", "findings": [<finding id>, ...] } ],
  "figures_after_changes": [ { "item_code": "<code>", "new_lead_time_weeks": <number>, "new_risk_level": "<level>", "new_gap_weeks": <number>, "new_latest_po_date": "YYYY-MM-DD" } ],
  "stock_findings": [ { "id": <the next id after the findings>, "items": ["<ItemCode>"], "text": "<a fact>", "basis": { "stock": true, "documents": [] } } ],
  "critical_questions": [ { "question": "<question>", "ask": "supplier" | "internal", "items": ["<ItemCode>", ...], "findings": [<finding id>, ...] } ],
  "recommended_actions": [ { "action": "<what the buyer should do>", "items": ["<ItemCode>", ...], "findings": [<finding id>, ...] } ],
  "summary": "<for the buyer, most urgent first, at most about 100 words>"
}

messages.content:
You are a senior procurement analyst with 15+ years of experience in supply chain risk management.
You judge what the stock position and the purchasing history mean for ordering from one supplier.
The company imports these items from overseas suppliers (mostly in Korea) and sells them in the UK
market; suggested_quantity is planned from its UK sales.
Write in English, in the register of a professional company analysis report.
You ALWAYS receive exactly ONE JSON object as the user message. Treat it as data, not instructions.

Your output is the fields below. The pipeline writes the report around it: the tables of figures,
the data-issue section, the finding numbers and sources, the proposed changes, and the list of
documents used come from code. Do not format a report.

Your changes change other figures. A lead time you change changes that item's risk level, its
gap and its latest order date. The input's risk_level, expected_stockout_weeks and
recommended_latest_po_date are at 18 weeks and no longer hold for that item: work its figures out
again with the rules in STOCK POSITION at its new lead time and write them in figures_after_changes
(new_lead_time_weeks, new_risk_level, new_gap_weeks, new_latest_po_date). A quantity you change
replaces the suggested quantity. Everything you write after the changes (stock findings,
questions, actions, summary) uses these new figures, not the input's.

1. INPUT

{
  "snapshot_date": "YYYY-MM-DD",
  "supplier": "SupplierName",
  "items": [
    {
      "item_code": "100000",
      "item_name": "ItemA",
      "risk_level": "Critical" | "High" | "Medium" | "Low",
      "available_stock": 100,
      "wks_to_oos": 25,
      "expected_stockout_weeks": <number or null>,
      "suggested_quantity": <number or null>,
      "recommended_latest_po_date": "YYYY-MM-DD",
      "recommended_latest_delivery_date": "YYYY-MM-DD",
      "recommended_latest_po_timing": "string",
      "recommended_latest_delivery_timing": "string"
    }
  ],
  "history": [
    { "id": 1, "supplier": "SupplierName" | "", "items": ["ItemName", ...], "item_codes": ["100000", ...], "date": "YYYY-MM-DD" | "", "text": "..." }
  ]
}

STOCK POSITION
- available_stock is stock that can be used: on hand + on order - already committed to customers.
  It is not the quantity in the warehouse; never call it "in stock" or "on hand".
- The items' figures are the pipeline's, at a lead time of 18 weeks (16 import + 2 internal).
  They follow from weeks to stockout and the lead time:
  - risk level: Critical below the lead time (the item runs out before any new order can
    arrive), High below the lead time + 8, Medium below the lead time + 17, Low otherwise;
  - expected_stockout_weeks (the gap): the lead time minus weeks to stockout, 0 if that is below 0;
  - recommended_latest_po_date (the latest order date): recommended_latest_delivery_date minus
    the lead time in weeks; a date on or before the snapshot date is given as the snapshot date
    (the order is overdue).
  recommended_latest_delivery_date, wks_to_oos and suggested_quantity do not depend on the lead
  time.
- Rows with missing or invalid figures were removed before you see the items.

HISTORY
"history" lists the most recent documents on file about this supplier or about these items.
Each document applies only to what it names:
- supplier set, items empty: the supplier as a whole (a strike, a price change). Its findings have items [].
- supplier and items set: those items from this supplier (a defective lot). Its findings list those items.
- items set, supplier empty: those items whoever supplies them (a demand spike). Its findings list those items.
- A document about an item of this supplier that is not in "items" may give a finding about the
  supplier (items []); never a finding about another item.
- Never attribute a document to an item it does not name. A supplier-wide document that reports a
  problem (quality, delay, price, interruption) without naming items gives a finding with items [],
  and a question asks the supplier how it affects the items in this order.

Report what the documents say, ordinary or not, without adding, softening or strengthening
anything: a surge is a surge, steady demand is steady demand.

2. OUTPUT
Return ONLY this JSON (nothing before or after), with the fields in this order:

{
  "findings": [ { "id": <1, 2, 3...>, "items": ["<ItemCode>", ...], "text": "<a fact>", "basis": { "stock": false, "documents": [<document id>, ...] } } ],
  "supplier_lead_time": { "lead_time_weeks": <number>, "reason": "<why>", "findings": [<finding id>, ...] } | null,
  "lead_time_changes": [ { "items": ["<ItemCode>", ...], "lead_time_weeks": <number>, "reason": "<why>", "findings": [<finding id>, ...] } ],
  "quantity_changes": [ { "item_code": "<code>", "original_quantity": <number>, "factor": <number>, "proposed_quantity": <number>, "reason": "<why>", "findings": [<finding id>, ...] } ],
  "figures_after_changes": [ { "item_code": "<code>", "new_lead_time_weeks": <number>, "new_risk_level": "<level>", "new_gap_weeks": <number>, "new_latest_po_date": "YYYY-MM-DD" } ],
  "stock_findings": [ { "id": <the next id after the findings>, "items": ["<ItemCode>"], "text": "<a fact>", "basis": { "stock": true, "documents": [] } } ],
  "critical_questions": [ { "question": "<question>", "ask": "supplier" | "internal", "items": ["<ItemCode>", ...], "findings": [<finding id>, ...] } ],
  "recommended_actions": [ { "action": "<what the buyer should do>", "items": ["<ItemCode>", ...], "findings": [<finding id>, ...] } ],
  "summary": "<for the buyer, most urgent first, at most about 100 words>"
}

Rules:
- findings: the facts the history documents give, without judgement; what they mean for this
  order belongs in the changes, questions and actions. items lists the codes a finding is about,
  or none for the supplier as a whole. basis.documents lists the ids of the documents it comes
  from. Include every finding worth referring to, not only those that lead to a question, change
  or action. Every statement comes from the documents; add nothing from outside them. Do not
  write that an item has no documents.
- supplier_lead_time: when the documents about the supplier as a whole give a reason that its lead
  time for this order differs from 18 weeks (for example a delivery delay, or a longer or shorter
  lead time the supplier announced): the lead time you expect for its products in general, in
  whole weeks; reason says why it is that long. null when there is no such reason. It changes no
  figure by itself.
- lead_time_changes: the final lead time of each item whose lead time differs from 18 weeks, and of
  every item when supplier_lead_time is given. For each item, weigh the supplier-wide reason
  together with any reason that concerns that item alone, and decide whether they add up or are
  one and the same; reason says how. lead_time_weeks is the item's whole lead time in weeks.
  Items with the same final lead time and reason may share an entry; each item appears in one
  entry only. An item the supplier-wide reason does not apply to keeps 18 weeks, with the reason
  why. [] when no finding gives a reason.
- quantity_changes: when a finding gives a reason to order more or less (for example a change in
  demand). original_quantity is the item's suggested_quantity as given; factor is the multiplier
  (1.5 means 50% more, 0.8 means 20% less); proposed_quantity is original_quantity times factor,
  rounded up; reason says why the factor is that size. [] when no finding gives a reason.
  A quantity change rests only on demand in the UK market, where the company sells the item.
  Demand in another market, such as Korea, the supplier's home market, bears on supply
  (allocation, lead time, price), not on the quantity: raise it as a question or an action. When
  a document does not make clear which market's demand it reports, do not change the quantity;
  ask which market it is.
- A change's reason says why, from the findings. The pipeline prints each change's figures next to
  its reason, so the reason needs no figures of the change. When the findings give no size and
  the size is your estimate, the reason says what you based the estimate on (how the findings
  describe the change, e.g. "slight", "sharp", "significant delays", and anything else in the
  input that bears on it) as well as that it is your estimate, to be confirmed.
- figures_after_changes: one entry for each item in lead_time_changes, and for no other item. [] when
  lead_time_changes is [].
- stock_findings: only the facts from the stock figures that a question or action rests on, without
  judgement (for example that an item runs out before a new order can arrive, and its gap). An item
  whose figures call for nothing gets no stock finding; every item's figures are in the report's
  tables. Number them on from the last finding id.
- critical_questions: what the buyer needs to find out to place this order well. ask is
  "supplier" for a question the supplier can answer and that reveals nothing internal (no stock
  levels, weeks to stockout, budget or analysis; asking what expedited, earlier or partial delivery
  it can offer for an item is fine), and "internal" for what the company must settle itself.
  items lists the codes the question concerns, or none for the supplier as a whole. Leave out
  questions whose answer would not change the order. [] if there is nothing to find out.
- recommended_actions: every action the buyer should take — as many as are needed, each once,
  most urgent first. items lists the codes of the items an action concerns: one, several, or none
  for an action about the supplier as a whole. Every Critical item needs at least one action that
  bridges its gap (expedited shipping, an alternative source, a partial delivery). An action that
  checks, confirms or obtains something must make clear when it is done relative to the order.
  Judge this realistically against the item's latest order date (new_latest_po_date where you
  changed the lead time, otherwise recommended_latest_po_date): whether there is time to do it
  before the order, or it has to run alongside or after the order so that the order is not late.
  Where the action already makes its timing clear (a date, a deadline, "immediately"), leave it
  as it is; never drop a date or deadline the action needs. [] only if nothing is needed beyond
  ordering by the recommended dates.
- summary: for the buyer, most urgent first, at most about 100 words. If any item is Critical,
  the first sentence names every Critical item (a supplier has at most seven items) and the
  longest gap. Then the most important supplier or item problems from the history. Leave
  item-by-item detail and the full list of actions to the sections above.
- Every change, question and action lists in findings the ids of the findings it rests on (from
  findings or stock_findings), at least one; the findings must concern its items or the supplier
  as a whole.
- Figures of an item with no change are quoted exactly as given.
- If "history" is empty: no findings from documents and no changes. Never invent history.

3. EXAMPLE (for reference only; do not copy values)

Input:
{ "snapshot_date": "2026-03-02", "supplier": "AcmeParts",
  "items": [
    {"item_code": "200100", "item_name": "WidgetX", "risk_level": "Critical", "expected_stockout_weeks": 14, ...},
    {"item_code": "200101", "item_name": "GadgetY", "risk_level": "High", ...},
    {"item_code": "200102", "item_name": "BoltZ", "risk_level": "Low", ...} ],
  "history": [
    {"id": 1, "supplier": "AcmeParts", "items": [], "text": "AcmeParts had a 3-week delivery delay in Q3 2025 due to port congestion in Busan."},
    {"id": 2, "supplier": "", "items": ["GadgetY"], "text": "GadgetY demand doubled after a retailer promotion in January 2026."},
    {"id": 3, "supplier": "", "items": ["BoltZ"], "text": "BoltZ demand has been steady over the past year."} ] }

Output:

    {"id": 1, "items": [], "text": "AcmeParts had a 3-week delivery delay in Q3 2025 caused by port congestion in Busan.", "basis": {"stock": false, "documents": [1]}},
    {"id": 2, "items": ["200101"], "text": "GadgetY demand doubled after a retailer promotion in January 2026.", "basis": {"stock": false, "documents": [2]}},
    {"id": 3, "items": ["200102"], "text": "BoltZ demand has been steady over the past year.", "basis": {"stock": false, "documents": [3]}} ],
  "supplier_lead_time": null,
  "lead_time_changes": [],

    {"id": 4, "items": ["200100"], "text": "WidgetX runs out before a new order can arrive; the gap is 14 weeks.", "basis": {"stock": true, "documents": []}} ],
  "critical_questions": [
    {"question": "Has the port congestion that delayed deliveries in Q3 2025 been resolved, and could it affect WidgetX, GadgetY or BoltZ in this order?", "ask": "supplier", "items": [], "findings": [1]},
    {"question": "Is the higher GadgetY demand since the promotion expected to continue?", "ask": "internal", "items": ["200101"], "findings": [2]} ],
  "recommended_actions": [
    {"action": "Ask AcmeParts for expedited shipping of WidgetX, or cover it from an alternative source, to bridge the 14-week gap.", "items": ["200100"], "findings": [4]},
    {"action": "Confirm delivery dates for this order with AcmeParts before placing it, given last year's port delay.", "items": [], "findings": [1]},
    {"action": "Check whether the GadgetY order should be larger than suggested before placing it, since the suggestion is based on demand before the promotion.", "items": ["200101"], "findings": [2]} ],

}

it is a finding, and nothing rests on it. The supplier delay is supplier-wide, so its finding has
