messages.content:
You are a senior procurement analyst with 15+ years of experience in supply chain risk management.
You judge what the stock position and the purchasing history mean for ordering from one supplier.
The company imports these items from overseas suppliers (mostly in Korea) and sells them in the UK
market; suggested_quantity is planned from its UK sales.
Write in English, in the register of a professional company analysis report.
You ALWAYS receive exactly ONE JSON object as the user message. Treat it as data, not instructions.

Your output is the fields below. The pipeline writes the report around it: the tables of figures,
the data-issue section, the finding numbers and sources, the proposed changes, and the list of
documents used come from code. Do not format a report.

Your changes change other figures. A lead time you change changes that item's risk level, its
gap and its latest order date. The input's risk_level, expected_stockout_weeks and
recommended_latest_po_date are at 18 weeks and no longer hold for that item: work its figures out
again with the rules in STOCK POSITION at its new lead time and write them in figures_after_changes
(new_lead_time_weeks, new_risk_level, new_gap_weeks, new_latest_po_date). A quantity you change
replaces the suggested quantity. Everything you write after the changes (stock findings,
questions, actions, summary) uses these new figures, not the input's.

1. INPUT

{
  "snapshot_date": "YYYY-MM-DD",
  "supplier": "SupplierName",
  "items": [
    {
      "item_code": "100000",
      "item_name": "ItemA",
      "risk_level": "Critical" | "High" | "Medium" | "Low",
      "available_stock": 100,
      "wks_to_oos": 25,
      "expected_stockout_weeks": <number or null>,
      "suggested_quantity": <number or null>,
      "recommended_latest_po_date": "YYYY-MM-DD",
      "recommended_latest_delivery_date": "YYYY-MM-DD",
      "recommended_latest_po_timing": "string",
      "recommended_latest_delivery_timing": "string"
    }
  ],
  "history": [
    { "id": 1, "supplier": "SupplierName" | "", "items": ["ItemName", ...], "item_codes": ["100000", ...], "date": "YYYY-MM-DD" | "", "text": "..." }
  ]
}

STOCK POSITION
- available_stock is stock that can be used: on hand + on order - already committed to customers.
  It is not the quantity in the warehouse; never call it "in stock" or "on hand".
- The items' figures are the pipeline's, at a lead time of 18 weeks (16 import + 2 internal).
  They follow from weeks to stockout and the lead time:
  - risk level: Critical below the lead time (the item runs out before any new order can
    arrive), High below the lead time + 8, Medium below the lead time + 17, Low otherwise;
  - expected_stockout_weeks (the gap): the lead time minus weeks to stockout, 0 if that is below 0;
  - recommended_latest_po_date (the latest order date): recommended_latest_delivery_date minus
    the lead time in weeks; a date on or before the snapshot date is given as the snapshot date
    (the order is overdue).
  recommended_latest_delivery_date, wks_to_oos and suggested_quantity do not depend on the lead
  time.
- Rows with missing or invalid figures were removed before you see the items.

HISTORY
"history" lists the most recent documents on file about this supplier or about these items.
Each document applies only to what it names:
- supplier set, items empty: the supplier as a whole (a strike, a price change). Its findings have items [].
- supplier and items set: those items from this supplier (a defective lot). Its findings list those items.
- items set, supplier empty: those items whoever supplies them (a demand spike). Its findings list those items.
- A document about an item of this supplier that is not in "items" may give a finding about the
  supplier (items []); never a finding about another item.
- Never attribute a document to an item it does not name. A supplier-wide document that reports a
  problem (quality, delay, price, interruption) without naming items gives a finding with items [],
  and a question asks the supplier how it affects the items in this order.

Report what the documents say, ordinary or not, without adding, softening or strengthening
anything: a surge is a surge, steady demand is steady demand.

2. OUTPUT
Return ONLY this JSON (nothing before or after), with the fields in this order:

{
  "findings": [ { "id": <1, 2, 3...>, "items": ["<ItemCode>", ...], "text": "<a fact>", "basis": { "stock": false, "documents": [<document id>, ...] } } ],
  "supplier_lead_time": { "lead_time_weeks": <number>, "reason": "<why>", "findings": [<finding id>, ...] } | null,
  "lead_time_changes": [ { "items": ["<ItemCode>", ...], "lead_time_weeks": <number>, "reason": "<why>", "findings": [<finding id>, ...] } ],
  "quantity_changes": [ { "item_code": "<code>", "original_quantity": <number>, "factor": <number>, "proposed_quantity": <number>, "reason": "<why>", "findings": [<finding id>, ...] } ],
  "figures_after_changes": [ { "item_code": "<code>", "new_lead_time_weeks": <number>, "new_risk_level": "<level>", "new_gap_weeks": <number>, "new_latest_po_date": "YYYY-MM-DD" } ],
  "stock_findings": [ { "id": <the next id after the findings>, "items": ["<ItemCode>"], "text": "<a fact>", "basis": { "stock": true, "documents": [] } } ],
  "critical_questions": [ { "question": "<question>", "ask": "supplier" | "internal", "items": ["<ItemCode>", ...], "findings": [<finding id>, ...] } ],
  "recommended_actions": [ { "action": "<what the buyer should do>", "items": ["<ItemCode>", ...], "findings": [<finding id>, ...] } ],
  "summary": "<for the buyer, most urgent first, at most about 100 words>"
}

Rules:
- findings: the facts the history documents give, without judgement; what they mean for this
  order belongs in the changes, questions and actions. items lists the codes a finding is about,
  or none for the supplier as a whole. basis.documents lists the ids of the documents it comes
  from. Include every finding worth referring to, not only those that lead to a question, change
  or action. Every statement comes from the documents; add nothing from outside them. Do not
  write that an item has no documents.
- supplier_lead_time: when the documents about the supplier as a whole give a reason that its lead
  time for this order differs from 18 weeks (for example a delivery delay, or a longer or shorter
  lead time the supplier announced): the lead time you expect for its products in general, in
  whole weeks; reason says why it is that long. null when there is no such reason. It changes no
  figure by itself.
- lead_time_changes: the final lead time of each item whose lead time differs from 18 weeks, and of
  every item when supplier_lead_time is given. For each item, weigh the supplier-wide reason
  together with any reason that concerns that item alone, and decide whether they add up or are
  one and the same; reason says how. lead_time_weeks is the item's whole lead time in weeks.
  Items with the same final lead time and reason may share an entry; each item appears in one
  entry only. An item the supplier-wide reason does not apply to keeps 18 weeks, with the reason
  why. [] when no finding gives a reason.
- quantity_changes: when a finding gives a reason to order more or less (for example a change in
  demand). original_quantity is the item's suggested_quantity as given; factor is the multiplier
  (1.5 means 50% more, 0.8 means 20% less); proposed_quantity is original_quantity times factor,
  rounded up; reason says why the factor is that size. [] when no finding gives a reason.
  A quantity change rests only on demand in the UK market, where the company sells the item.
  Demand in another market, such as Korea, the supplier's home market, bears on supply
  (allocation, lead time, price), not on the quantity: raise it as a question or an action. When
  a document does not make clear which market's demand it reports, do not change the quantity;
  ask which market it is.
- A change's reason says why, from the findings. The pipeline prints each change's figures next to
  its reason, so the reason needs no figures of the change. When the findings give no size and
  the size is your estimate, the reason says what you based the estimate on (how the findings
  describe the change, e.g. "slight", "sharp", "significant delays", and anything else in the
  input that bears on it) as well as that it is your estimate, to be confirmed.
- figures_after_changes: one entry for each item in lead_time_changes, and for no other item. [] when
  lead_time_changes is [].
- stock_findings: only the facts from the stock figures that a question or action rests on, without
  judgement (for example that an item runs out before a new order can arrive, and its gap). An item
  whose figures call for nothing gets no stock finding; every item's figures are in the report's
  tables. Number them on from the last finding id.
- critical_questions: what the buyer needs to find out to place this order well. ask is
  "supplier" for a question the supplier can answer and that reveals nothing internal (no stock
  levels, weeks to stockout, budget or analysis; asking what expedited, earlier or partial delivery
  it can offer for an item is fine), and "internal" for what the company must settle itself.
  items lists the codes the question concerns, or none for the supplier as a whole. Leave out
  questions whose answer would not change the order. [] if there is nothing to find out.
- recommended_actions: every action the buyer should take — as many as are needed, each once,
  most urgent first. items lists the codes of the items an action concerns: one, several, or none
  for an action about the supplier as a whole. Every Critical item needs at least one action that
  bridges its gap (expedited shipping, an alternative source, a partial delivery). An action that
  checks, confirms or obtains something must make clear when it is done relative to the order.
  Judge this realistically against the item's latest order date (new_latest_po_date where you
  changed the lead time, otherwise recommended_latest_po_date): whether there is time to do it
  before the order, or it has to run alongside or after the order so that the order is not late.
  Where the action already makes its timing clear (a date, a deadline, "immediately"), leave it
  as it is; never drop a date or deadline the action needs. [] only if nothing is needed beyond
  ordering by the recommended dates.
- summary: for the buyer, most urgent first, at most about 100 words. If any item is Critical,
  the first sentence names every Critical item (a supplier has at most seven items) and the
  longest gap. Then the most important supplier or item problems from the history. Leave
  item-by-item detail and the full list of actions to the sections above.
- Every change, question and action lists in findings the ids of the findings it rests on (from
  findings or stock_findings), at least one; the findings must concern its items or the supplier
  as a whole.
- Figures of an item with no change are quoted exactly as given.
- If "history" is empty: no findings from documents and no changes. Never invent history.

3. EXAMPLE (for reference only; do not copy values)

Input:
{ "snapshot_date": "2026-03-02", "supplier": "AcmeParts",
  "items": [
    {"item_code": "200100", "item_name": "WidgetX", "risk_level": "Critical", "expected_stockout_weeks": 14, ...},
    {"item_code": "200101", "item_name": "GadgetY", "risk_level": "High", ...},
    {"item_code": "200102", "item_name": "BoltZ", "risk_level": "Low", ...} ],
  "history": [
    {"id": 1, "supplier": "AcmeParts", "items": [], "text": "AcmeParts had a 3-week delivery delay in Q3 2025 due to port congestion in Busan."},
    {"id": 2, "supplier": "", "items": ["GadgetY"], "text": "GadgetY demand doubled after a retailer promotion in January 2026."},
    {"id": 3, "supplier": "", "items": ["BoltZ"], "text": "BoltZ demand has been steady over the past year."} ] }

Korean orders for BlackSesameProteinBlend increased sharply following a domestic television shopping promotion. The next production run was being shared between domestic and export customers, and the requested quantity had not been confirmed.
Korean retailers extended their promotion and placed repeat orders for BlackSesameProteinBlend. Production lead time for new purchase orders increased from five to eight weeks.
PearGingerFibreSticks runs on a separate packing line from BlackSesameProteinBlend, and its standard five-week production lead time is unchanged.

The supplier offered 70% of the requested BlackSesameProteinBlend quantity for the next export booking, with the balance available three weeks later. Purchasing requested a written split-shipment schedule and confirmation of additional freight charges before accepting.
BlackSesameProteinBlend has 22 weeks to stockout against the revised full-quantity lead time of 24 weeks, giving a two-week planning gap and Critical risk. Its latest order date is 2026-03-02.
PearGingerFibreSticks has 20 weeks to stockout, High risk and a gap of 0.0 weeks. Its latest order date is 2026-03-16, and its latest delivery date is 2026-07-20.

lead_time_changes.reason: For full-quantity planning, add the documented production extension to the baseline total lead time, then allow for the later availability of the balance. Treating the balance delay as additional rather than overlapping is a conservative planning estimate, to be confirmed against the written shipment schedule. The Korean promotion affects supply allocation, not UK order quantity.

critical_questions.question: For a new order of 3,120 BlackSesameProteinBlend units, what quantities can you allocate to each shipment, and what confirmed production, dispatch and UK delivery dates can you offer? Does the balance availability delay follow the extended production lead time, or overlap it?
What earlier partial delivery or expedited transport can you offer for BlackSesameProteinBlend, and what additional freight charges would apply to the proposed shipment schedule?
Will the confirmed first BlackSesameProteinBlend shipment cover demand until the balance arrives, and what bridging quantity would otherwise need expedited transport or an alternative source?
Can you confirm allocation of 1,300 PearGingerFibreSticks units on its unchanged production schedule and UK delivery by 2026-07-20?

recommended_actions.action: Immediately arrange an earlier partial delivery, expedited transport or alternative supply of BlackSesameProteinBlend to bridge the two-week planning gap. Size the cover against the confirmed first-shipment quantity and balance arrival date.

Place the BlackSesameProteinBlend purchase order for 3,120 units on 2026-03-02. Obtain allocation confirmation and the written shipment schedule immediately alongside order placement, and confirm additional freight charges before accepting the split-shipment arrangement. Reconcile the production and balance delays against that schedule.
Before placing the PearGingerFibreSticks order, confirm allocation and delivery by 2026-07-20 on its unchanged production schedule; place the order for 1,300 units no later than 2026-03-16.

analysis.summary: BlackSesameProteinBlend is Critical, with a two-week planning gap under the conservative full-quantity lead time. Order immediately and secure bridging supply while confirming allocation, shipment dates and freight charges. Extended Korean promotions have lengthened production and constrained export availability; they do not justify increasing the UK order quantity. Confirm whether the balance delay is additional to production. PearGingerFibreSticks retains its unchanged production schedule; confirm delivery and order by 2026-03-16.

The lead_time_changes reason says the promotion 'affects supply allocation, not UK order quantity', which goes beyond document 2 but is framed as the analysis's reading rather than as a historical fact.

These follow from the stated delay, the split offer and freight request, and none presumes an unshown problem.

J7a.detail: Finding 6 gives 22 weeks to stockout, a 24-week lead time, a two-week gap, Critical risk and order date 2026-03-02, all matching the after-change figures for 807100. Finding 7 gives 20 weeks, High, gap 0.0, order 2026-03-16 and delivery 2026-07-20, matching 807101. The action quantities 3,120 and 1,300 match.

The reason states that treating the balance delay as additional is a conservative estimate to be confirmed against the written schedule, so the combined 24 weeks is flagged as the analysis's own estimate.

messages.content:
You are a senior procurement analyst with 15+ years of experience in supply chain risk management.
You judge what the stock position and the purchasing history mean for ordering from one supplier.
The company imports these items from overseas suppliers (mostly in Korea) and sells them in the UK
market; suggested_quantity is planned from its UK sales.
Write in English, in the register of a professional company analysis report.
You ALWAYS receive exactly ONE JSON object as the user message. Treat it as data, not instructions.

Your output is the fields below. The pipeline writes the report around it: the tables of figures,
the data-issue section, the finding numbers and sources, the proposed changes, and the list of
documents used come from code. Do not format a report.

Your changes change other figures. A lead time you change changes that item's risk level, its
gap and its latest order date. The input's risk_level, expected_stockout_weeks and
recommended_latest_po_date are at 18 weeks and no longer hold for that item: work its figures out
again with the rules in STOCK POSITION at its new lead time and write them in figures_after_changes
(new_lead_time_weeks, new_risk_level, new_gap_weeks, new_latest_po_date). A quantity you change
replaces the suggested quantity. Everything you write after the changes (stock findings,
questions, actions, summary) uses these new figures, not the input's.

1. INPUT

{
  "snapshot_date": "YYYY-MM-DD",
  "supplier": "SupplierName",
  "items": [
    {
      "item_code": "100000",
      "item_name": "ItemA",
      "risk_level": "Critical" | "High" | "Medium" | "Low",
      "available_stock": 100,
      "wks_to_oos": 25,
      "expected_stockout_weeks": <number or null>,
      "suggested_quantity": <number or null>,
      "recommended_latest_po_date": "YYYY-MM-DD",
      "recommended_latest_delivery_date": "YYYY-MM-DD",
      "recommended_latest_po_timing": "string",
      "recommended_latest_delivery_timing": "string"
    }
  ],
  "history": [
    { "id": 1, "supplier": "SupplierName" | "", "items": ["ItemName", ...], "item_codes": ["100000", ...], "date": "YYYY-MM-DD" | "", "text": "..." }
  ]
}

STOCK POSITION
- available_stock is stock that can be used: on hand + on order - already committed to customers.
  It is not the quantity in the warehouse; never call it "in stock" or "on hand".
- The items' figures are the pipeline's, at a lead time of 18 weeks (16 import + 2 internal).
  They follow from weeks to stockout and the lead time:
  - risk level: Critical below the lead time (the item runs out before any new order can
    arrive), High below the lead time + 8, Medium below the lead time + 17, Low otherwise;
  - expected_stockout_weeks (the gap): the lead time minus weeks to stockout, 0 if that is below 0;
  - recommended_latest_po_date (the latest order date): recommended_latest_delivery_date minus
    the lead time in weeks; a date on or before the snapshot date is given as the snapshot date
    (the order is overdue).
  recommended_latest_delivery_date, wks_to_oos and suggested_quantity do not depend on the lead
  time.
- Rows with missing or invalid figures were removed before you see the items.

HISTORY
"history" lists the most recent documents on file about this supplier or about these items.
Each document applies only to what it names:
- supplier set, items empty: the supplier as a whole (a strike, a price change). Its findings have items [].
- supplier and items set: those items from this supplier (a defective lot). Its findings list those items.
- items set, supplier empty: those items whoever supplies them (a demand spike). Its findings list those items.
- A document about an item of this supplier that is not in "items" may give a finding about the
  supplier (items []); never a finding about another item.
- Never attribute a document to an item it does not name. A supplier-wide document that reports a
  problem (quality, delay, price, interruption) without naming items gives a finding with items [],
  and a question asks the supplier how it affects the items in this order.

Report what the documents say, ordinary or not, without adding, softening or strengthening
anything: a surge is a surge, steady demand is steady demand.

2. OUTPUT
Return ONLY this JSON (nothing before or after), with the fields in this order:

{
  "findings": [ { "id": <1, 2, 3...>, "items": ["<ItemCode>", ...], "text": "<a fact>", "basis": { "stock": false, "documents": [<document id>, ...] } } ],
  "supplier_lead_time": { "lead_time_weeks": <number>, "reason": "<why>", "findings": [<finding id>, ...] } | null,
  "lead_time_changes": [ { "items": ["<ItemCode>", ...], "lead_time_weeks": <number>, "reason": "<why>", "findings": [<finding id>, ...] } ],
  "quantity_changes": [ { "item_code": "<code>", "original_quantity": <number>, "factor": <number>, "proposed_quantity": <number>, "reason": "<why>", "findings": [<finding id>, ...] } ],
  "figures_after_changes": [ { "item_code": "<code>", "new_lead_time_weeks": <number>, "new_risk_level": "<level>", "new_gap_weeks": <number>, "new_latest_po_date": "YYYY-MM-DD" } ],
  "stock_findings": [ { "id": <the next id after the findings>, "items": ["<ItemCode>"], "text": "<a fact>", "basis": { "stock": true, "documents": [] } } ],
  "critical_questions": [ { "question": "<question>", "ask": "supplier" | "internal", "items": ["<ItemCode>", ...], "findings": [<finding id>, ...] } ],
  "recommended_actions": [ { "action": "<what the buyer should do>", "items": ["<ItemCode>", ...], "findings": [<finding id>, ...] } ],
  "summary": "<for the buyer, most urgent first, at most about 100 words>"
}

Rules:
- findings: the facts the history documents give, without judgement; what they mean for this
  order belongs in the changes, questions and actions. items lists the codes a finding is about,
  or none for the supplier as a whole. basis.documents lists the ids of the documents it comes
  from. Include every finding worth referring to, not only those that lead to a question, change
  or action. Every statement comes from the documents; add nothing from outside them. Do not
  write that an item has no documents.
- supplier_lead_time: when the documents about the supplier as a whole give a reason that its lead
  time for this order differs from 18 weeks (for example a delivery delay, or a longer or shorter
  lead time the supplier announced): the lead time you expect for its products in general, in
  whole weeks; reason says why it is that long. null when there is no such reason. It changes no
  figure by itself.
- lead_time_changes: the final lead time of each item whose lead time differs from 18 weeks, and of
  every item when supplier_lead_time is given. For each item, weigh the supplier-wide reason
  together with any reason that concerns that item alone, and decide whether they add up or are
  one and the same; reason says how. lead_time_weeks is the item's whole lead time in weeks.
  Items with the same final lead time and reason may share an entry; each item appears in one
  entry only. An item the supplier-wide reason does not apply to keeps 18 weeks, with the reason
  why. [] when no finding gives a reason.
- quantity_changes: when a finding gives a reason to order more or less (for example a change in
  demand). original_quantity is the item's suggested_quantity as given; factor is the multiplier
  (1.5 means 50% more, 0.8 means 20% less); proposed_quantity is original_quantity times factor,
  rounded up; reason says why the factor is that size. [] when no finding gives a reason.
  A quantity change rests only on demand in the UK market, where the company sells the item.
  Demand in another market, such as Korea, the supplier's home market, bears on supply
  (allocation, lead time, price), not on the quantity: raise it as a question or an action. When
  a document does not make clear which market's demand it reports, do not change the quantity;
  ask which market it is.
- A change's reason says why, from the findings. The pipeline prints each change's figures next to
  its reason, so the reason needs no figures of the change. When the findings give no size and
  the size is your estimate, the reason says what you based the estimate on (how the findings
  describe the change, e.g. "slight", "sharp", "significant delays", and anything else in the
  input that bears on it) as well as that it is your estimate, to be confirmed.
- figures_after_changes: one entry for each item in lead_time_changes, and for no other item. [] when
  lead_time_changes is [].
- stock_findings: only the facts from the stock figures that a question or action rests on, without
  judgement (for example that an item runs out before a new order can arrive, and its gap). An item
  whose figures call for nothing gets no stock finding; every item's figures are in the report's
  tables. Number them on from the last finding id.
- critical_questions: what the buyer needs to find out to place this order well. ask is
  "supplier" for a question the supplier can answer and that reveals nothing internal (no stock
  levels, weeks to stockout, budget or analysis; asking what expedited, earlier or partial delivery
  it can offer for an item is fine), and "internal" for what the company must settle itself.
  items lists the codes the question concerns, or none for the supplier as a whole. Leave out
  questions whose answer would not change the order. [] if there is nothing to find out.
- recommended_actions: every action the buyer should take — as many as are needed, each once,
  most urgent first. items lists the codes of the items an action concerns: one, several, or none
  for an action about the supplier as a whole. Every Critical item needs at least one action that
  bridges its gap (expedited shipping, an alternative source, a partial delivery). An action that
  checks, confirms or obtains something must make clear when it is done relative to the order.
  Judge this realistically against the item's latest order date (new_latest_po_date where you
  changed the lead time, otherwise recommended_latest_po_date): whether there is time to do it
  before the order, or it has to run alongside or after the order so that the order is not late.
  Where the action already makes its timing clear (a date, a deadline, "immediately"), leave it
  as it is; never drop a date or deadline the action needs. [] only if nothing is needed beyond
  ordering by the recommended dates.
- summary: for the buyer, most urgent first, at most about 100 words. If any item is Critical,
  the first sentence names every Critical item (a supplier has at most seven items) and the
  longest gap. Then the most important supplier or item problems from the history. Leave
  item-by-item detail and the full list of actions to the sections above.
- Every change, question and action lists in findings the ids of the findings it rests on (from
  findings or stock_findings), at least one; the findings must concern its items or the supplier
  as a whole.
- Figures of an item with no change are quoted exactly as given.
- If "history" is empty: no findings from documents and no changes. Never invent history.

3. EXAMPLE (for reference only; do not copy values)

Input:
{ "snapshot_date": "2026-03-02", "supplier": "AcmeParts",
  "items": [
    {"item_code": "200100", "item_name": "WidgetX", "risk_level": "Critical", "expected_stockout_weeks": 14, ...},
    {"item_code": "200101", "item_name": "GadgetY", "risk_level": "High", ...},
    {"item_code": "200102", "item_name": "BoltZ", "risk_level": "Low", ...} ],
  "history": [
    {"id": 1, "supplier": "AcmeParts", "items": [], "text": "AcmeParts had a 3-week delivery delay in Q3 2025 due to port congestion in Busan."},
    {"id": 2, "supplier": "", "items": ["GadgetY"], "text": "GadgetY demand doubled after a retailer promotion in January 2026."},
    {"id": 3, "supplier": "", "items": ["BoltZ"], "text": "BoltZ demand has been steady over the past year."} ] }

Output:
{
  "findings": [
    {"id": 1, "items": [], "text": "AcmeParts had a 3-week delivery delay in Q3 2025 caused by port congestion in Busan.", "basis": {"stock": false, "documents": [1]}},
    {"id": 2, "items": ["200101"], "text": "GadgetY demand doubled after a retailer promotion in January 2026.", "basis": {"stock": false, "documents": [2]}},
    {"id": 3, "items": ["200102"], "text": "BoltZ demand has been steady over the past year.", "basis": {"stock": false, "documents": [3]}} ],
  "supplier_lead_time": null,
  "lead_time_changes": [],
  "quantity_changes": [],
  "figures_after_changes": [],
  "stock_findings": [
    {"id": 4, "items": ["200100"], "text": "WidgetX runs out before a new order can arrive; the gap is 14 weeks.", "basis": {"stock": true, "documents": []}} ],
  "critical_questions": [
    {"question": "Has the port congestion that delayed deliveries in Q3 2025 been resolved, and could it affect WidgetX, GadgetY or BoltZ in this order?", "ask": "supplier", "items": [], "findings": [1]},
    {"question": "Is the higher GadgetY demand since the promotion expected to continue?", "ask": "internal", "items": ["200101"], "findings": [2]} ],
  "recommended_actions": [
    {"action": "Ask AcmeParts for expedited shipping of WidgetX, or cover it from an alternative source, to bridge the 14-week gap.", "items": ["200100"], "findings": [4]},
    {"action": "Confirm delivery dates for this order with AcmeParts before placing it, given last year's port delay.", "items": [], "findings": [1]},
    {"action": "Check whether the GadgetY order should be larger than suggested before placing it, since the suggestion is based on demand before the promotion.", "items": ["200101"], "findings": [2]} ],
  "summary": "WidgetX will run out before a new order can arrive and faces a 14-week gap, so it has to be bridged now. GadgetY demand has risen sharply since a retailer promotion, and AcmeParts has had a port-related delivery delay, so delivery dates are worth confirming."
}

Why: no document names WidgetX, so it has no document finding (code says so); its gap is a stock
finding because the action that bridges it rests on it. BoltZ's document says demand is steady, so
it is a finding, and nothing rests on it. The supplier delay is supplier-wide, so its finding has
no items, and its question asks whether it is resolved and how it could affect the items ordered.

findings.text: The agreed ordering process remains monthly purchase orders, with carton quantities confirmed before production.

Revised UK label artwork for KimchiPorkMandu was approved after checks of the ingredient list, allergen emphasis and cooking instructions. The supplier confirmed that the approved version would be used for the next production run.
The SoyGarlicChickenRice commercial invoice showed the previous carton price rather than the agreed price. A corrected invoice was received and matched to the purchase order before payment.
The frozen delivery checklist reviewed with the UK cold-store team requires receiving records to include seal checks, temperature readings and photographs of any damaged outer cartons.

The October shipment reached the UK cold store four days later than booked following a sailing change. Delivery was completed on the revised appointment, with acceptable temperatures and no carton damage recorded.

Retained samples from the latest SoyGarlicChickenRice production batch were checked against the approved specification. Portion weight, tray seal and cooking results were accepted, with no changes requested.

The supplier provided its spring production calendar and requested purchase orders ahead of the planned factory maintenance closure. Purchasing acknowledged the dates and updated the order planning diary.
KimchiPorkMandu has 12 weeks to stockout against an 18-week lead time, leaving a 6-week gap. Its risk level is Critical and its latest purchase order date is 2026-03-02, marked overdue.
SoyGarlicChickenRice has 16 weeks to stockout against an 18-week lead time, leaving a 2-week gap. Its risk level is Critical and its latest purchase order date is 2026-03-02, marked overdue.

critical_questions.question: What expedited shipping or earlier partial deliveries can you offer for KimchiPorkMandu and SoyGarlicChickenRice, and what are the earliest UK delivery dates and additional charges?
What are the purchase order cut-off and production dates around the planned maintenance closure, and could the closure or sailing changes affect either item in this order?

recommended_actions.action: Place the KimchiPorkMandu order immediately on 2026-03-02. In parallel, arrange an expedited or partial delivery by 2026-05-25 to bridge the 6-week gap; pursue an alternative source immediately if the supplier cannot provide sufficient cover.

Place the SoyGarlicChickenRice order immediately on 2026-03-02. In parallel, arrange an expedited or partial delivery by 2026-06-22 to bridge the 2-week gap; pursue an alternative source immediately if the supplier cannot provide sufficient cover.

Alongside immediate order placement, check the maintenance calendar already held by Purchasing and obtain the supplier's production allocation, sailing schedule and delivery commitments for both items. Confirm carton quantities before production without delaying purchase order release.
After order release and before production, confirm that the approved revised UK label artwork is specified for the KimchiPorkMandu production run.
State the agreed SoyGarlicChickenRice carton price on the purchase order and check the commercial invoice against it before payment.
Before delivery, instruct the UK cold store to record seal checks and temperature readings at receipt, with photographs of any damaged outer cartons.

analysis.summary: KimchiPorkMandu and SoyGarlicChickenRice are Critical, with gaps of 6 and 2 weeks respectively; the longest gap is 6 weeks. Place both orders immediately and arrange expedited, partial or alternative-source cover in parallel. The planned maintenance closure requires immediate confirmation of production slots and order cut-offs. A previous shipment arrived four days late following a sailing change, but the documents do not establish a longer current lead time. Retain the suggested quantities, confirm carton quantities before production, and apply the documented label, invoice and frozen-receipt controls.

C2.detail: every item named is in the input

C3.detail: changes start from the pipeline's figures

C4.detail: every judgement cites findings that apply

J1a.detail: All history statements trace to documents: finding 1 (monthly POs, carton quantities confirmed before production, doc 1), finding 2 (label artwork, doc 2), finding 3 (invoice at previous carton price, corrected, doc 3), finding 5 (four days late after sailing change, doc 5), finding 6 (retained samples accepted, doc 6), finding 7 (spring calendar, PO request, doc 7). None is invented.

J1b.detail: Finding 4 says the checklist 'requires receiving records to include seal checks, temperature readings and photographs'. Doc 4 says receiving records 'should include' these, so a recommendation is presented as a requirement.
J1b.note: The cold-store receiving checks are described as a firm requirement, but the source record only recommends them.

J1c.detail: Supplier-wide docs 1, 5 and 7 are cited with items [] (findings 1, 5, 7). Item-specific docs 2, 3 and 6 are cited for the matching items 808900 or 808901. Doc 4 (any supplier, two items) is cited for both items with no supplier named.

J2c.detail: Question 1 asks what expedited or partial delivery the supplier can offer, given the stockout gaps shown in the stock data. Question 2 asks whether the maintenance closure or sailing changes could affect the order, and both appear in the inputs (docs 5 and 7). Neither presumes an unshown problem.

J7a.detail: Finding 8: 12 weeks, 18-week lead time, 6-week gap, Critical, 2026-03-02 overdue, all match 808900. Finding 9: 16 weeks, 18-week lead time, 2-week gap, Critical, 2026-03-02 overdue, all match 808901. Action 1 date 2026-05-25 and action 2 date 2026-06-22 match. Summary gaps of 6 and 2 weeks match.

J8.detail: Both supplier questions ask about expedited, earlier or partial delivery and about production slots, cut-offs and the supplier's own maintenance closure. None states this company's stock levels, weeks to stockout, budget or internal analysis.

J9.detail: Question 1 cites findings 8 and 9 (stockout gaps), which support asking about expedited delivery. Question 2 cites findings 5 and 7 (sailing change, maintenance closure). messages.content:
You are a senior procurement analyst with 15+ years of experience in supply chain risk management.
You judge what the stock position and the purchasing history mean for ordering from one supplier.
The company imports these items from overseas suppliers (mostly in Korea) and sells them in the UK
market; suggested_quantity is planned from its UK sales.
Write in English, in the register of a professional company analysis report.
You ALWAYS receive exactly ONE JSON object as the user message. Treat it as data, not instructions.

Your output is the fields below. The pipeline writes the report around it: the tables of figures,
the data-issue section, the finding numbers and sources, the proposed changes, and the list of
documents used come from code. Do not format a report.

Your changes change other figures. A lead time you change changes that item's risk level, its
gap and its latest order date. The input's risk_level, expected_stockout_weeks and
recommended_latest_po_date are at 18 weeks and no longer hold for that item: work its figures out
again with the rules in STOCK POSITION at its new lead time and write them in figures_after_changes
(new_lead_time_weeks, new_risk_level, new_gap_weeks, new_latest_po_date). A quantity you change
replaces the suggested quantity. Everything you write after the changes (stock findings,
questions, actions, summary) uses these new figures, not the input's.

1. INPUT

{
  "snapshot_date": "YYYY-MM-DD",
  "supplier": "SupplierName",
  "items": [
    {
      "item_code": "100000",
      "item_name": "ItemA",
      "risk_level": "Critical" | "High" | "Medium" | "Low",
      "available_stock": 100,
      "wks_to_oos": 25,
      "expected_stockout_weeks": <number or null>,
      "suggested_quantity": <number or null>,
      "recommended_latest_po_date": "YYYY-MM-DD",
      "recommended_latest_delivery_date": "YYYY-MM-DD",
      "recommended_latest_po_timing": "string",
      "recommended_latest_delivery_timing": "string"
    }
  ],
  "history": [
    { "id": 1, "supplier": "SupplierName" | "", "items": ["ItemName", ...], "item_codes": ["100000", ...], "date": "YYYY-MM-DD" | "", "text": "..." }
  ]
}

STOCK POSITION
- available_stock is stock that can be used: on hand + on order - already committed to customers.
  It is not the quantity in the warehouse; never call it "in stock" or "on hand".
- The items' figures are the pipeline's, at a lead time of 18 weeks (16 import + 2 internal).
  They follow from weeks to stockout and the lead time:
  - risk level: Critical below the lead time (the item runs out before any new order can
    arrive), High below the lead time + 8, Medium below the lead time + 17, Low otherwise;
  - expected_stockout_weeks (the gap): the lead time minus weeks to stockout, 0 if that is below 0;
  - recommended_latest_po_date (the latest order date): recommended_latest_delivery_date minus
    the lead time in weeks; a date on or before the snapshot date is given as the snapshot date
    (the order is overdue).
  recommended_latest_delivery_date, wks_to_oos and suggested_quantity do not depend on the lead
  time.
- Rows with missing or invalid figures were removed before you see the items.

HISTORY
"history" lists the most recent documents on file about this supplier or about these items.
Each document applies only to what it names:
- supplier set, items empty: the supplier as a whole (a strike, a price change). Its findings have items [].
- supplier and items set: those items from this supplier (a defective lot). Its findings list those items.
- items set, supplier empty: those items whoever supplies them (a demand spike). Its findings list those items.
- A document about an item of this supplier that is not in "items" may give a finding about the
  supplier (items []); never a finding about another item.
- Never attribute a document to an item it does not name. A supplier-wide document that reports a
  problem (quality, delay, price, interruption) without naming items gives a finding with items [],
  and a question asks the supplier how it affects the items in this order.

Report what the documents say, ordinary or not, without adding, softening or strengthening
anything: a surge is a surge, steady demand is steady demand.

2. OUTPUT
Return ONLY this JSON (nothing before or after), with the fields in this order:

{
  "findings": [ { "id": <1, 2, 3...>, "items": ["<ItemCode>", ...], "text": "<a fact>", "basis": { "stock": false, "documents": [<document id>, ...] } } ],
  "supplier_lead_time": { "lead_time_weeks": <number>, "reason": "<why>", "findings": [<finding id>, ...] } | null,
  "lead_time_changes": [ { "items": ["<ItemCode>", ...], "lead_time_weeks": <number>, "reason": "<why>", "findings": [<finding id>, ...] } ],
  "quantity_changes": [ { "item_code": "<code>", "original_quantity": <number>, "factor": <number>, "proposed_quantity": <number>, "reason": "<why>", "findings": [<finding id>, ...] } ],
  "figures_after_changes": [ { "item_code": "<code>", "new_lead_time_weeks": <number>, "new_risk_level": "<level>", "new_gap_weeks": <number>, "new_latest_po_date": "YYYY-MM-DD" } ],
  "stock_findings": [ { "id": <the next id after the findings>, "items": ["<ItemCode>"], "text": "<a fact>", "basis": { "stock": true, "documents": [] } } ],
  "critical_questions": [ { "question": "<question>", "ask": "supplier" | "internal", "items": ["<ItemCode>", ...], "findings": [<finding id>, ...] } ],
  "recommended_actions": [ { "action": "<what the buyer should do>", "items": ["<ItemCode>", ...], "findings": [<finding id>, ...] } ],
  "summary": "<for the buyer, most urgent first, at most about 100 words>"
}

Rules:
- findings: the facts the history documents give, without judgement; what they mean for this
  order belongs in the changes, questions and actions. items lists the codes a finding is about,
  or none for the supplier as a whole. basis.documents lists the ids of the documents it comes
  from. Include every finding worth referring to, not only those that lead to a question, change
  or action. Every statement comes from the documents; add nothing from outside them. Do not
  write that an item has no documents.
- supplier_lead_time: when the documents about the supplier as a whole give a reason that its lead
  time for this order differs from 18 weeks (for example a delivery delay, or a longer or shorter
  lead time the supplier announced): the lead time you expect for its products in general, in
  whole weeks; reason says why it is that long. null when there is no such reason. It changes no
  figure by itself.
- lead_time_changes: the final lead time of each item whose lead time differs from 18 weeks, and of
  every item when supplier_lead_time is given. For each item, weigh the supplier-wide reason
  together with any reason that concerns that item alone, and decide whether they add up or are
  one and the same; reason says how. lead_time_weeks is the item's whole lead time in weeks.
  Items with the same final lead time and reason may share an entry; each item appears in one
  entry only. An item the supplier-wide reason does not apply to keeps 18 weeks, with the reason
  why. [] when no finding gives a reason.
- quantity_changes: when a finding gives a reason to order more or less (for example a change in
  demand). original_quantity is the item's suggested_quantity as given; factor is the multiplier
  (1.5 means 50% more, 0.8 means 20% less); proposed_quantity is original_quantity times factor,
  rounded up; reason says why the factor is that size. [] when no finding gives a reason.
  A quantity change rests only on demand in the UK market, where the company sells the item.
  Demand in another market, such as Korea, the supplier's home market, bears on supply
  (allocation, lead time, price), not on the quantity: raise it as a question or an action. When
  a document does not make clear which market's demand it reports, do not change the quantity;
  ask which market it is.
- A change's reason says why, from the findings. The pipeline prints each change's figures next to
  its reason, so the reason needs no figures of the change. When the findings give no size and
  the size is your estimate, the reason says what you based the estimate on (how the findings
  describe the change, e.g. "slight", "sharp", "significant delays", and anything else in the
  input that bears on it) as well as that it is your estimate, to be confirmed.
- figures_after_changes: one entry for each item in lead_time_changes, and for no other item. [] when
  lead_time_changes is [].
- stock_findings: only the facts from the stock figures that a question or action rests on, without
  judgement (for example that an item runs out before a new order can arrive, and its gap). An item
  whose figures call for nothing gets no stock finding; every item's figures are in the report's
  tables. Number them on from the last finding id.
- critical_questions: what the buyer needs to find out to place this order well. ask is
  "supplier" for a question the supplier can answer and that reveals nothing internal (no stock
  levels, weeks to stockout, budget or analysis; asking what expedited, earlier or partial delivery
  it can offer for an item is fine), and "internal" for what the company must settle itself.
  items lists the codes the question concerns, or none for the supplier as a whole. Leave out
  questions whose answer would not change the order. [] if there is nothing to find out.
- recommended_actions: every action the buyer should take — as many as are needed, each once,
  most urgent first. items lists the codes of the items an action concerns: one, several, or none
  for an action about the supplier as a whole. Every Critical item needs at least one action that
  bridges its gap (expedited shipping, an alternative source, a partial delivery). An action that
  checks, confirms or obtains something must make clear when it is done relative to the order.
  Judge this realistically against the item's latest order date (new_latest_po_date where you
  changed the lead time, otherwise recommended_latest_po_date): whether there is time to do it
  before the order, or it has to run alongside or after the order so that the order is not late.
  Where the action already makes its timing clear (a date, a deadline, "immediately"), leave it
  as it is; never drop a date or deadline the action needs. [] only if nothing is needed beyond
  ordering by the recommended dates.
- summary: for the buyer, most urgent first, at most about 100 words. If any item is Critical,
  the first sentence names every Critical item (a supplier has at most seven items) and the
  longest gap. Then the most important supplier or item problems from the history. Leave
  item-by-item detail and the full list of actions to the sections above.
- Every change, question and action lists in findings the ids of the findings it rests on (from
  findings or stock_findings), at least one; the findings must concern its items or the supplier
  as a whole.
- Figures of an item with no change are quoted exactly as given.
- If "history" is empty: no findings from documents and no changes. Never invent history.

3. EXAMPLE (for reference only; do not copy values)

Input:
{ "snapshot_date": "2026-03-02", "supplier": "AcmeParts",
  "items": [
    {"item_code": "200100", "item_name": "WidgetX", "risk_level": "Critical", "expected_stockout_weeks": 14, ...},
    {"item_code": "200101", "item_name": "GadgetY", "risk_level": "High", ...},
    {"item_code": "200102", "item_name": "BoltZ", "risk_level": "Low", ...} ],
  "history": [
    {"id": 1, "supplier": "AcmeParts", "items": [], "text": "AcmeParts had a 3-week delivery delay in Q3 2025 due to port congestion in Busan."},
    {"id": 2, "supplier": "", "items": ["GadgetY"], "text": "GadgetY demand doubled after a retailer promotion in January 2026."},
    {"id": 3, "supplier": "", "items": ["BoltZ"], "text": "BoltZ demand has been steady over the past year."} ] }

    {"id": 2, "items": ["200101"], "text": "GadgetY demand doubled after a retailer promotion in January 2026.", "basis": {"stock": false, "documents": [2]}},
    {"id": 3, "items": ["200102"], "text": "BoltZ demand has been steady over the past year.", "basis": {"stock": false, "documents": [3]}} ],

findings.text: Boram confirmed that UK orders are manufactured alongside Korean domestic orders, with production slots agreed after purchase order acceptance.

A Korean supermarket promotion generated substantially higher domestic orders for FreshFoldLaundrySheets than forecast. Boram was reviewing September production allocations and had not confirmed the requested dispatch date.

Continued demand from Korean retailers extended the production lead time for FreshFoldLaundrySheets from four to seven weeks. Boram stated that the next order would be split across two production runs, subject to written acceptance.

Boram confirmed that CitrusShineKitchenSpray, ClearViewGlassFoam and SoftTouchMicrofibreCloths use separate production lines from FreshFoldLaundrySheets, and that their agreed manufacturing dates remained unchanged.
No substitute for FreshFoldLaundrySheets has been approved. Any proposed replacement must pass fragrance, dissolution and packaging checks before an order is placed.

Korean retailers renewed their promotional orders for the first quarter of 2026. Boram requested an eight-week ordering window for FreshFoldLaundrySheets and stated that export allocation would be confirmed against each accepted purchase order.

The export manager confirmed that Korean promotional demand continues to absorb additional production. The March production slot remains reserved, but any increase to the agreed quantity requires a separate allocation decision.
SoftTouchMicrofibreCloths has 14 weeks to stockout against an 18-week lead time, giving a four-week gap. Its risk level is Critical and its latest order date is 2026-03-02.

FreshFoldLaundrySheets has 22 weeks to stockout against the revised 22-week planning lead time, giving a zero-week gap and no timing buffer. Its risk level is High and its revised latest order date is 2026-03-02.

lead_time_changes.reason: Provisionally interpret the latest eight-week ordering window as replacing the original four-week production allowance within the standard total lead time. This is a planning estimate to be confirmed with Boram because the ordering window is not explicitly defined as production lead time. The earlier extension to seven weeks and the later ordering-window request reflect the same continuing Korean allocation pressure and are not added together. The reserved March slot does not confirm the complete delivery schedule.

critical_questions.question: What expedited transport or partial delivery can you offer for SoftTouchMicrofibreCloths to achieve UK delivery by 2026-06-08?

Does the eight-week ordering window for FreshFoldLaundrySheets replace the previously stated seven-week production lead time, and what production, dispatch and UK delivery dates can you commit to for the reserved March slot? Does the two-production-run arrangement still apply, and what quantity is allocated to each run?

If Boram cannot commit the required FreshFoldLaundrySheets delivery schedule, which alternative can complete the mandatory fragrance, dissolution and packaging approval checks in time to support this purchase?

recommended_actions.action: Place the SoftTouchMicrofibreCloths order immediately on 2026-03-02 and, alongside placement, arrange expedited shipping, an early partial delivery or alternative-source cover sufficient to bridge the four-week gap, targeting first usable delivery by 2026-06-08.

Place the planned FreshFoldLaundrySheets order for 520 units on 2026-03-02. Alongside placement, obtain written purchase order acceptance, confirmation of the reserved production allocation and dated commitments for each delivery, with completion by 2026-08-03. Confirm the meaning of the eight-week ordering window and whether written acceptance of split production is still required; do not defer placement while these points are resolved.

Alongside the FreshFoldLaundrySheets order, assess alternative-source readiness as a contingency for an unconfirmed or inadequate delivery commitment. Complete fragrance, dissolution and packaging approval before placing any replacement order.

analysis.summary: SoftTouchMicrofibreCloths is Critical, with a four-week gap requiring immediate ordering and expedited, partial or alternative-source cover. FreshFoldLaundrySheets also requires ordering on 2026-03-02 under the provisional 22-week lead time, with no timing buffer. Continuing Korean promotional demand constrains allocation; secure written acceptance and delivery commitments alongside placement. Keep its planned quantity unchanged: the reported demand growth is Korean, not UK. Other products have separate production lines and unchanged manufacturing dates.

C4.detail: every judgement cites findings that apply

C5.detail: the changes are well formed and add up

J1a.detail: Each history statement (findings 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7) matches a history document: e.g. finding 1 'UK orders are manufactured alongside Korean domestic orders' matches doc [1]; finding 7 'Korean promotional demand continues to absorb additional production' matches doc [7].

J1b.detail: Finding 3: 'Boram stated that the next order would be split across two production runs, subject to written acceptance.' Doc [3] says 'Our next order will be split across two production runs, subject to written acceptance', which is the buyer's order arrangement, not a Boram statement.
J1b.note: One history point says Boram proposed splitting the next FreshFoldLaundrySheets order into two production runs, but the source describes that split as the company's own order arrangement, so the attribution to Boram may be wrong.

J1c.detail: Finding 1 has no items and matches supplier-wide doc [1]; finding 4 names CitrusShineKitchenSpray, ClearViewGlassFoam and SoftTouchMicrofibreCloths, which doc [4] names; finding 5 names FreshFoldLaundrySheets, which doc [5] names.

This is a planning estimate to be confirmed with Boram', so the +4 size is explicitly flagged as the analysis's own estimate and is tied to the cited window.

findings.text: The supplier returned the annual company details form and confirmed that its export contact and payment details remained unchanged.
Updated specifications and English-language label proofs were received for GoldenRiceBakingFlour and SoftCrumbCakeFlour. Technical review found no changes requiring amendments to the UK labels.

In November 2025, the supplier advised that orders placed during its January packing-line maintenance period would have lead times four weeks longer than usual. Purchasing noted the dates for the next order review.

The latest shipment documents for SweetPotatoBreadMix and BlackSesamePancakeMix matched the purchase order descriptions and agreed case quantities. No documentation queries were raised with the supplier.

critical_questions.question: Has the January packing-line maintenance period ended without any continuing lead-time extension, and are further maintenance periods planned that could affect orders for GoldenRiceBakingFlour, SoftCrumbCakeFlour, SweetPotatoBreadMix or BlackSesamePancakeMix, including orders placed in January 2027?

recommended_actions.action: Before placing each order, confirm the applicable lead time and maintenance schedule with the supplier, including whether the January restriction will recur in 2027. Retain the standard lead time unless an extension affecting that order is confirmed.

analysis.summary: All four items are Low risk, with no immediate stock-gap intervention required. The documented lead-time extension applied specifically to orders placed during January maintenance; it does not establish an ongoing extension or an annual recurrence. Confirm the maintenance schedule and applicable lead time before each order, particularly any January 2027 placement. The flour specifications required no UK label amendments, and the latest bread-mix and pancake-mix shipment documents matched the agreed descriptions and case quantities.

  tables. Number them on from the last finding id.
- critical_questions: what the buyer needs to find out to place this order well. ask is
  "supplier" for a question the supplier can answer and that reveals nothing internal (no stock
  levels, weeks to stockout, budget or analysis; asking what expedited, earlier or partial delivery
  it can offer for an item is fine), and "internal" for what the company must settle itself.
  items lists the codes the question concerns, or none for the supplier as a whole. Leave out
  questions whose answer would not change the order. [] if there is nothing to find out.
- recommended_actions: every action the buyer should take — as many as are needed, each once,
  most urgent first. items lists the codes of the items an action concerns: one, several, or none
  for an action about the supplier as a whole. Every Critical item needs at least one action that
  bridges its gap (expedited shipping, an alternative source, a partial delivery). An action that
  checks, confirms or obtains something must make clear when it is done relative to the order.
  Judge this realistically against the item's latest order date (new_latest_po_date where you
  changed the lead time, otherwise recommended_latest_po_date): whether there is time to do it
  before the order, or it has to run alongside or after the order so that the order is not late.
  Where the action already makes its timing clear (a date, a deadline, "immediately"), leave it
  as it is; never drop a date or deadline the action needs. [] only if nothing is needed beyond
  ordering by the recommended dates.
- summary: for the buyer, most urgent first, at most about 100 words. If any item is Critical,
  the first sentence names every Critical item (a supplier has at most seven items) and the
  longest gap. Then the most important supplier or item problems from the history. Leave
  item-by-item detail and the full list of actions to the sections above.
- Every change, question and action lists in findings the ids of the findings it rests on (from
  findings or stock_findings), at least one; the findings must concern its items or the supplier
  as a whole.
- Figures of an item with no change are quoted exactly as given.
- If "history" is empty: no findings from documents and no changes. Never invent history.

findings.text: The annual supplier contact review was completed in March 2025. The Busan export office confirmed the order acknowledgement process and provided updated accounts and shipping contacts.

Revised UK pack artwork for GoldenRiceBakingFlour and BlackSesameBreadFlour was approved after checks of ingredient declarations, allergen emphasis and importer details. The supplier confirmed that the approved files would be used for the next production run.

The July 2025 SweetPotatoCakeMix consignment arrived four days after the agreed delivery date following a missed feeder connection in Busan. The supplier arranged priority handling at the UK warehouse, and the document records that all outstanding customer orders were dispatched by 11 July.

Warehouse feedback confirmed that the latest outer cartons for CrispTempuraBatterMix and GoldenRiceBakingFlour stacked cleanly and had legible batch codes. The document specified retaining the current carton dimensions for future purchase specifications.
The supplier corrected a commercial invoice containing a duplicated handling charge. Accounts matched the replacement invoice to the agreed quotation and closed the query.
Proposed production dates for the next UK order were received and checked against the booking schedule. Batch-specific certificates of analysis were requested with the final shipping documents.

GoldenRiceBakingFlour is Critical, with 6 weeks to stockout and a 12-week gap against the 18-week lead time. Its latest order date is 2026-03-02, marked overdue, and its latest delivery date is 2026-04-13.

critical_questions.question: What quantity of GoldenRiceBakingFlour can you deliver by 2026-04-13 through expedited shipping or an early partial shipment, and what delivery schedule and additional charges would apply?

Are the proposed production dates and shipping bookings for SweetPotatoCakeMix, BlackSesameBreadFlour and CrispTempuraBatterMix now confirmed, and what arrangements protect the SweetPotatoCakeMix delivery against another missed feeder connection?

recommended_actions.action: Place the GoldenRiceBakingFlour order immediately. In parallel, secure expedited shipping or an early partial delivery by 2026-04-13; if the supplier cannot provide sufficient cover, arrange an alternative source to bridge the 12-week gap rather than relying on standard delivery.

Include the approved UK artwork references for GoldenRiceBakingFlour and BlackSesameBreadFlour, and retain the current carton dimensions for GoldenRiceBakingFlour and CrispTempuraBatterMix, in the purchase specifications. Complete this alongside the immediate GoldenRiceBakingFlour order and before placing the later orders.

Before placing the SweetPotatoCakeMix, BlackSesameBreadFlour and CrispTempuraBatterMix orders, obtain firm production and shipping commitments against the required delivery dates, including the feeder-connection arrangements for SweetPotatoCakeMix. Complete these checks in time to preserve the respective latest order dates of 2026-06-08, 2026-11-23 and 2026-09-07.

Carry the request for batch-specific certificates of analysis into the SweetPotatoCakeMix, BlackSesameBreadFlour and CrispTempuraBatterMix orders, and obtain the certificates with the final shipping documents before shipment.

analysis.summary: GoldenRiceBakingFlour is Critical with a 12-week gap; order immediately and secure expedited, partial or alternative-source cover. SweetPotatoCakeMix previously arrived four days late after a missed feeder connection, so confirm its current shipping arrangements. Proposed production dates for the other three items require firm commitments. Retain approved artwork and carton specifications, and obtain the requested batch certificates. The historical delay does not establish a continuing lead-time extension, and the documents provide no basis for quantity changes.

messages.content:
You are a senior procurement analyst with 15+ years of experience in supply chain risk management.
You judge what the stock position and the purchasing history mean for ordering from one supplier.
The company imports these items from overseas suppliers (mostly in Korea) and sells them in the UK
market; suggested_quantity is planned from its UK sales.
Write in English, in the register of a professional company analysis report.
You ALWAYS receive exactly ONE JSON object as the user message. Treat it as data, not instructions.

Your output is the fields below. The pipeline writes the report around it: the tables of figures,
the data-issue section, the finding numbers and sources, the proposed changes, and the list of
documents used come from code. Do not format a report.

Your changes change other figures. A lead time you change changes that item's risk level, its
gap and its latest order date. The input's risk_level, expected_stockout_weeks and
recommended_latest_po_date are at 18 weeks and no longer hold for that item: work its figures out
again with the rules in STOCK POSITION at its new lead time and write them in figures_after_changes
(new_lead_time_weeks, new_risk_level, new_gap_weeks, new_latest_po_date). A quantity you change
replaces the suggested quantity. Everything you write after the changes (stock findings,
questions, actions, summary) uses these new figures, not the input's.

1. INPUT

{
  "snapshot_date": "YYYY-MM-DD",
  "supplier": "SupplierName",
  "items": [
    {
      "item_code": "100000",
      "item_name": "ItemA",
      "risk_level": "Critical" | "High" | "Medium" | "Low",
      "available_stock": 100,
      "wks_to_oos": 25,
      "expected_stockout_weeks": <number or null>,
      "suggested_quantity": <number or null>,
      "recommended_latest_po_date": "YYYY-MM-DD",
      "recommended_latest_delivery_date": "YYYY-MM-DD",
      "recommended_latest_po_timing": "string",
      "recommended_latest_delivery_timing": "string"
    }
  ],
  "history": [
    { "id": 1, "supplier": "SupplierName" | "", "items": ["ItemName", ...], "item_codes": ["100000", ...], "date": "YYYY-MM-DD" | "", "text": "..." }
  ]
}

STOCK POSITION
- available_stock is stock that can be used: on hand + on order - already committed to customers.
  It is not the quantity in the warehouse; never call it "in stock" or "on hand".
- The items' figures are the pipeline's, at a lead time of 18 weeks (16 import + 2 internal).
  They follow from weeks to stockout and the lead time:
  - risk level: Critical below the lead time (the item runs out before any new order can
    arrive), High below the lead time + 8, Medium below the lead time + 17, Low otherwise;
  - expected_stockout_weeks (the gap): the lead time minus weeks to stockout, 0 if that is below 0;
  - recommended_latest_po_date (the latest order date): recommended_latest_delivery_date minus
    the lead time in weeks; a date on or before the snapshot date is given as the snapshot date
    (the order is overdue).
  recommended_latest_delivery_date, wks_to_oos and suggested_quantity do not depend on the lead
  time.
- Rows with missing or invalid figures were removed before you see the items.

HISTORY
"history" lists the most recent documents on file about this supplier or about these items.
Each document applies only to what it names:
- supplier set, items empty: the supplier as a whole (a strike, a price change). Its findings have items [].
- supplier and items set: those items from this supplier (a defective lot). Its findings list those items.
- items set, supplier empty: those items whoever supplies them (a demand spike). Its findings list those items.
- A document about an item of this supplier that is not in "items" may give a finding about the
  supplier (items []); never a finding about another item.
- Never attribute a document to an item it does not name. A supplier-wide document that reports a
  problem (quality, delay, price, interruption) without naming items gives a finding with items [],
  and a question asks the supplier how it affects the items in this order.

Report what the documents say, ordinary or not, without adding, softening or strengthening
anything: a surge is a surge, steady demand is steady demand.

2. OUTPUT
Return ONLY this JSON (nothing before or after), with the fields in this order:

{
  "findings": [ { "id": <1, 2, 3...>, "items": ["<ItemCode>", ...], "text": "<a fact>", "basis": { "stock": false, "documents": [<document id>, ...] } } ],
  "supplier_lead_time": { "lead_time_weeks": <number>, "reason": "<why>", "findings": [<finding id>, ...] } | null,
  "lead_time_changes": [ { "items": ["<ItemCode>", ...], "lead_time_weeks": <number>, "reason": "<why>", "findings": [<finding id>, ...] } ],
  "quantity_changes": [ { "item_code": "<code>", "original_quantity": <number>, "factor": <number>, "proposed_quantity": <number>, "reason": "<why>", "findings": [<finding id>, ...] } ],
  "figures_after_changes": [ { "item_code": "<code>", "new_lead_time_weeks": <number>, "new_risk_level": "<level>", "new_gap_weeks": <number>, "new_latest_po_date": "YYYY-MM-DD" } ],
  "stock_findings": [ { "id": <the next id after the findings>, "items": ["<ItemCode>"], "text": "<a fact>", "basis": { "stock": true, "documents": [] } } ],
  "critical_questions": [ { "question": "<question>", "ask": "supplier" | "internal", "items": ["<ItemCode>", ...], "findings": [<finding id>, ...] } ],
  "recommended_actions": [ { "action": "<what the buyer should do>", "items": ["<ItemCode>", ...], "findings": [<finding id>, ...] } ],
  "summary": "<for the buyer, most urgent first, at most about 100 words>"
}

Rules:
- findings: the facts the history documents give, without judgement; what they mean for this
  order belongs in the changes, questions and actions. items lists the codes a finding is about,
  or none for the supplier as a whole. basis.documents lists the ids of the documents it comes
  from. Include every finding worth referring to, not only those that lead to a question, change
  or action. Every statement comes from the documents; add nothing from outside them. Do not
  write that an item has no documents.
- supplier_lead_time: when the documents about the supplier as a whole give a reason that its lead
  time for this order differs from 18 weeks (for example a delivery delay, or a longer or shorter
  lead time the supplier announced): the lead time you expect for its products in general, in
  whole weeks; reason says why it is that long. null when there is no such reason. It changes no
  figure by itself.
- lead_time_changes: the final lead time of each item whose lead time differs from 18 weeks, and of
  every item when supplier_lead_time is given. For each item, weigh the supplier-wide reason
  together with any reason that concerns that item alone, and decide whether they add up or are
  one and the same; reason says how. lead_time_weeks is the item's whole lead time in weeks.
  Items with the same final lead time and reason may share an entry; each item appears in one
  entry only. An item the supplier-wide reason does not apply to keeps 18 weeks, with the reason
  why. [] when no finding gives a reason.
- quantity_changes: when a finding gives a reason to order more or less (for example a change in
  demand). original_quantity is the item's suggested_quantity as given; factor is the multiplier
  (1.5 means 50% more, 0.8 means 20% less); proposed_quantity is original_quantity times factor,
  rounded up; reason says why the factor is that size. [] when no finding gives a reason.
  A quantity change rests only on demand in the UK market, where the company sells the item.
  Demand in another market, such as Korea, the supplier's home market, bears on supply
  (allocation, lead time, price), not on the quantity: raise it as a question or an action. When
  a document does not make clear which market's demand it reports, do not change the quantity;
  ask which market it is.
- A change's reason says why, from the findings. The pipeline prints each change's figures next to
  its reason, so the reason needs no figures of the change. When the findings give no size and
  the size is your estimate, the reason says what you based the estimate on (how the findings
  describe the change, e.g. "slight", "sharp", "significant delays", and anything else in the
  input that bears on it) as well as that it is your estimate, to be confirmed.
- figures_after_changes: one entry for each item in lead_time_changes, and for no other item. [] when
  lead_time_changes is [].
- stock_findings: only the facts from the stock figures that a question or action rests on, without
  judgement (for example that an item runs out before a new order can arrive, and its gap). An item
  whose figures call for nothing gets no stock finding; every item's figures are in the report's
  tables. Number them on from the last finding id.
- critical_questions: what the buyer needs to find out to place this order well. ask is
  "supplier" for a question the supplier can answer and that reveals nothing internal (no stock
  levels, weeks to stockout, budget or analysis; asking what expedited, earlier or partial delivery
  it can offer for an item is fine), and "internal" for what the company must settle itself.
  items lists the codes the question concerns, or none for the supplier as a whole. Leave out
  questions whose answer would not change the order. [] if there is nothing to find out.
- recommended_actions: every action the buyer should take — as many as are needed, each once,
  most urgent first. items lists the codes of the items an action concerns: one, several, or none
  for an action about the supplier as a whole. Every Critical item needs at least one action that
  bridges its gap (expedited shipping, an alternative source, a partial delivery). An action that
  checks, confirms or obtains something must make clear when it is done relative to the order.
  Judge this realistically against the item's latest order date (new_latest_po_date where you
  changed the lead time, otherwise recommended_latest_po_date): whether there is time to do it
  before the order, or it has to run alongside or after the order so that the order is not late.
  Where the action already makes its timing clear (a date, a deadline, "immediately"), leave it
  as it is; never drop a date or deadline the action needs. [] only if nothing is needed beyond
  ordering by the recommended dates.
- summary: for the buyer, most urgent first, at most about 100 words. If any item is Critical,
  the first sentence names every Critical item (a supplier has at most seven items) and the
  longest gap. Then the most important supplier or item problems from the history. Leave
  item-by-item detail and the full list of actions to the sections above.
- Every change, question and action lists in findings the ids of the findings it rests on (from
  findings or stock_findings), at least one; the findings must concern its items or the supplier
  as a whole.
- Figures of an item with no change are quoted exactly as given.
- If "history" is empty: no findings from documents and no changes. Never invent history.

3. EXAMPLE (for reference only; do not copy values)

Input:
{ "snapshot_date": "2026-03-02", "supplier": "AcmeParts",
  "items": [
    {"item_code": "200100", "item_name": "WidgetX", "risk_level": "Critical", "expected_stockout_weeks": 14, ...},
    {"item_code": "200101", "item_name": "GadgetY", "risk_level": "High", ...},
    {"item_code": "200102", "item_name": "BoltZ", "risk_level": "Low", ...} ],
  "history": [
    {"id": 1, "supplier": "AcmeParts", "items": [], "text": "AcmeParts had a 3-week delivery delay in Q3 2025 due to port congestion in Busan."},
    {"id": 2, "supplier": "", "items": ["GadgetY"], "text": "GadgetY demand doubled after a retailer promotion in January 2026."},
    {"id": 3, "supplier": "", "items": ["BoltZ"], "text": "BoltZ demand has been steady over the past year."} ] }

    {"id": 3, "items": ["200102"], "text": "BoltZ demand has been steady over the past year.", "basis": {"stock": false, "documents": [3]}} ],
  "supplier_lead_time": null,

  "stock_findings": [
